stories.title: Wilbon taking leave of absence from ESPN to address health issues
stories.summary: Michael Wilbon, the longtime ESPN commentator and co-host of "Pardon the Interruption," is taking a leave of absence to address health issues.
stories.detailText: Michael Wilbon is taking a break. The longtime ESPN commentator and co-host of the network's popular "Pardon the Interruption" talk show alongside good friend Tony Kornheiser announced Monday that he is taking a leave of absence because of what he described as "multiple health issues." Wilbon, who turns 68 later this month, wrote in a post on X that he is taking a trip to "the injured list" but added that he hopes it is "not an extended one." While Wilbon, who is also featured on ESPN's NBA coverage, declined to go into detail about what he is facing, he added that there are people in his personal life who noticed "worrisome signs" in recent years that he largely ignored. Wilbon did make a point to note the issues are not alcohol- or gambling-related. "I have no idea how exactly this part of my journey will wind up," Wilbon posted. "The goal is to come out of it feeling much better than I do now and ready to return to sparring with Tony." Wilbon's last appearance on "PTI," which recently celebrated its 25th anniversary and is credited with revolutionizing television's "sports debate" format, was Oct. 26. The show, in part, is a byproduct of the friendship of Wilbon and Kornheiser, who became colleagues at The Washington Post in the 1980s. "I have loved sparring and hosting PTI with Tony every single day these past 25 years," Wilbon wrote. "And I'm incredibly grateful for the support and encouragement of my colleagues as I take this time away to concentrate on me, especially my well-being."

stories.title: Coby White to make season debut for Hornets after missing team's first 7 games with strained calf
stories.summary: White signed a three-year deal with Charlotte after being acquired from the Bulls. Trading LaMelo Ball cleared a starting spot for him.
stories.detailText: The Charlotte Hornets are getting one piece of their projected starting guard tandem back in the lineup. Point guard Coby White was not listed on Monday's injury report, and the team announced he will make his 2026-27 season debut versus the Detroit Pistons. White, 26, strained his left calf during training camp, sidelining him through the preseason and the Hornets' first seven games of the regular season. In his absence, Dennis Schröder has played well, averaging 11.7 points and 5.4 assists. 🎙️ Coby White: "I'm super excited, feeling blessed to be able to play my first game tonight." "Our process has been really good in terms of creating open looks for each other and getting to our spots... the tide will turn and we'll start making shots." pic.twitter.com/tx0dSpBBBy — r/CharlotteHornets (@HornetsReddit) November 2, 2026 However, Charlotte presumably signed White to a 3-year, $74 million contract so he could be the starting point guard. The Hornets acquired White from the Chicago Bulls at last season's trade deadline, and in 21 games, he averaged 15.6 points with 3 assists while shooting 39% on 110 3-point attempts. In addition to re-signing White to a new contract, the Hornets made his role clear by trading point guard LaMelo Ball to the Minnesota Timberwolves in exchange for center Naz Reid, several draft picks and first-round swaps. White's best season was during the 2024-25 campaign when he took on more of a scoring role for the Bulls. He averaged 20.4 points and 4.5 assists, shooting 37% on a career-high 584 3-point shots. Over the past three seasons, White has scored 19.1 points per game with 4.6 assists and 3.9 rebounds. COBY WHITE AGAIN 🎯 HE BEATS THE Q3 BUZZER FROM DEEP! https://t.co/OsxMFRqBnR pic.twitter.com/WOE9fozbcx — NBA (@NBA) April 15, 2026 While he may not be as much of a scorer or playmaker as Ball, the Hornets are hoping White will be more consistent. The eight-year veteran has shot 52% or better during the past four seasons. Additionally, Charlotte is looking for Kon Knueppel to assume more of a playmaking role when he returns. Knueppel will comprise the other part of the Hornets' starting backcourt once he becomes available. He is out for Monday's game, but is close to returning from a strained left hamstring he sustained before training camp. Knueppel was assigned to the team's G League affiliate to practice last week before being recalled to the Hornets. Charlotte announced on Monday that the team picked up Knueppel's third-year option for $11 million. He also has a $13.9 million team option for 2027-28 as part of his four-year rookie contract. Following Monday's matchup with the Pistons, the Hornets (3-4) visit the Brooklyn Nets (1-5) on Wednesday and host the Boston Celtics (5-1) on Friday.

stories.title: Oklahoma City to retire Russell Westbrook's jersey in Feb. 7 ceremony
stories.summary: When James Harden and Kevin Durant left, it was Russell Westbrook who stayed and won in OKC.
stories.detailText: James Harden demanded a max contract and wouldn't budge, so Oklahoma City traded him to Houston. Kevin Durant left to form a super team in Golden State. Russell Westbrook stayed, collected triple-doubles at a historic rate, won an MVP, and forever became a hero to fans in Oklahoma City. Fittingly, the Thunder are going to retire his jersey on Feb. 7, a Sunday night game against the Knicks, a ceremony and a game you will be able to watch on NBC and stream on Peacock , part of Sunday Night Basketball. ❝Many players make an impact but only great players leave a legacy.❞ Thunder Set to Retire Russell Westbrook’s No. 0 on February 7, 2027 https://t.co/PZGINYXZiV pic.twitter.com/ABE9F21dSR — OKC THUNDER (@okcthunder) November 2, 2026 "Many players make an impact but only great players leave a legacy. Russell Westbrook's legacy was built both on the court and in the community," Thunder Executive Vice President Sam Presti said in a statement announcing the honor. "His mindset was relentless, his commitment deep. For all those reasons, Oklahomans consider him one of their own and his number will be raised to the rafters, in Oklahoma City forever." It was considered a bit of a reach, and a bet on his athleticism, when Presti drafted Westbrook No. 4 out of UCLA — a bet that paid off handsomely. Westbrook played 11 seasons in Oklahoma City and was key to the Thunder reaching their first NBA Finals in 2012. In those 11 seasons, the Thunder made the playoffs nine times and reached the Western Conference Finals four times. Westbrook's greatest season in Oklahoma City was the 2016-17, when he racked up 42 triple-doubles on his way to averaging 31.6 points, 10.7 rebounds and 10.4 assists — plus making a host of clutch plays for the team — and going on to win Most Valuable Player. Westbrook finished his career with 209 triple-doubles, the most in league history. Westbrook is a lock future Hall of Famer: An MVP and member of the NBA's 75th Anniversary Team, a nine-time All-NBA and All-Star, and a two-time scoring champion. "We are incredibly proud to retire Russell's number. Russell made a lasting mark on the city and state during his time with the team, and his involvement in the community has endured long after," Thunder Chairman Clayton I. Bennett said in a statement. "We are deeply grateful for his genuine care for the people of Oklahoma, and he will always be considered a member of the Oklahoma City community." That community will rally to celebrate him on Feb. 7.

stories.title: Thunder to retire Russell Westbrook's No. 0
stories.summary: The Thunder will retire Russell Westbrook's No. 0 this season. The former MVP played the first 11 of his 18 seasons in Oklahoma City.
stories.detailText: The Oklahoma City Thunder announced they will retire Russell Westbrook 's No. 0 in the rafters on Feb. 7. Westbrook was a first-round pick of the organization in 2008, just days before the team officially became the Thunder after relocating from Seattle. Westbrook played the first 11 years of his 18-season career in OKC and paired with Kevin Durant to turn the young Thunder into one of the best teams in the league. However, after Durant's free agent departure following the 2015-16 season, Westbrook's stature in Oklahoma City grew. The next season, Westbrook became the first player to average a triple-double for an entire season since Oscar Robertson, going for 31.6 points, 10.7 rebounds and 10.4 assists, and was named league MVP. He continued to average a triple-double for the following two seasons, his final ones with the Thunder. "Many players make an impact but only great players leave a legacy. Russell Westbrook's legacy was built both on the court and in the community," Thunder executive vice president and general manager Sam Presti said in a statement Monday. "His mindset was relentless, his commitment deep. For all those reasons, Oklahomans consider him one of their own and his number will be raised to the rafters, in Oklahoma City forever." OKC traded Westbrook to the Houston Rockets ahead of the 2019-20 season, part of an offseason that saw the team move away from the Westbrook- Paul George pairing and establish the foundation for the franchise's current run of success. After a season in Houston, Westbrook bounced around the league playing with the Washington Wizards , Los Angeles Lakers , LA Clippers , Denver Nuggets and Sacramento Kings . A nine-time All-Star and member of the NBA's 75th anniversary team in 2021, Westbrook announced his retirement this offseason. His No. 0 will be the second jersey retired by the Thunder joining Nick Collison's No. 4.

stories.title: Michael Jordan congratulates Valykries star Gabby Williams after WNBA title
stories.summary: His Airness had a simple message for the Golden State Valkyries star after her 30-point performance in Game 7.
stories.detailText: OAKLAND, Calif. -- As Gabby Williams scrolled through the endless congratulatory text messages she has received since winning the 2026 WNBA championship with the Golden State Valkyries on Saturday night, one stood out from the rest. It was from Michael Jordan. "Stay hungry," the text read, Williams told ESPN on Monday. She responded quickly: "I've never been hungrier." Williams, who was crowned WNBA Finals MVP, scored 30 points in the first Game 7 in WNBA history while wearing a pair of Air Jordan 41 sneakers. Twenty-eight of those points came in the second half. Williams also added a game-high four blocks plus two steals. The Chase Center and Bay Area are no strangers to incredible playoff performances. Some of those responsible for the memorable local area moments, including San Francisco Giants legend Barry Bonds and Golden State Warriors forward Draymond Green , were courtside to see Williams'. As Valkyries owner Joe Lacob tells it, even they were amazed. "Her second half ... legendary," Lacob said after the championship. "That was unbelievable stuff." Her teammates felt the same. "We've talked about it all season: We have Gabby Williams, and you don't," Valkyries guard Tiffany Hayes said at exit interviews Monday. "[It] was one of the greatest things I've ever seen. "She took it upon herself to make sure we weren't going to lose that game." Golden State guard Veronica Burton said it felt like she was in the stands with the Ballhalla crowd watching Williams, even though she was on the court with her. "You talk about being in the zone, and you hear about flow state, maybe you watch it on TV, but to be there in real time and to witness it was amazing," Burton said. Williams, though, said she hasn't reflected on her Game 7 heroics. She's just sleepy. "I'm just living in the moment," Williams said. "This was a really long month, a really long series. I've been focusing on my friends and my family, my loved ones and soaking this in with my teammates. "Unfortunately, I don't think we'll ever have this exact group again. So I am trying to soak in this moment as long as I can with these people."

stories.title: Jaylen Brown's favorite purchase? An 18th century harp
stories.summary: The Sixers guard's Boston apartment contains possession of some rare pieces.
stories.detailText: PHILADELPHIA -- 76ers forward Jaylen Brown -- who signed what was then the richest contract in NBA history three years ago -- said a golden harp in his Boston apartment is his most-cherished acquisition. "I think my best, my most favorite purchase," Brown told Atlanta rapper Lil Baby in an interview last month. Brown also discussed the prized possession in detail and gave a tour of his Boston apartment in an interview with Architectural Digest published Monday. As tunes from his harp played in the background, Brown told Lil Baby that it was made in the 18th century but that it was "reimagined" and is one of the most expensive pieces in his apartment. He thanked his harpist, Li Shan Tan, the principal harp for the New Haven Symphony Orchestra, for being "an amazing therapist." "Most of the time I use my harp, it's just me and my chef," Brown told Architectural Digest. "A memory raced through my head: me at the end of my 20s, with a harp [broken] in my unit. And how central it would be to the social hours of 10 p.m. to 4 a.m." At times, Brown tries to play the harp himself. "From time to time, when she is not around, I go and I try to re-create some sounds," Brown said. The Boston Celtics chose Brown with the No. 3 pick in the 2016 draft. After 10 seasons and a championship in 2024, the Celtics traded Brown to Philadelphia this offseason for Paul George , two first-round picks (2028, 2031) and two second-round selections (2028, 2030). "I grew up here age 19 to 29," Brown said. "I developed here in Boston as a young man. "There's been other places, but this one -- I created it, it was crafted by my vision. This one felt the most like home." Brown will play his former team Nov. 10 in Philadelphia.

stories.title: Grizzlies tore down their core. So how are they the NBA's last unbeaten team?
stories.summary: The Memphis Grizzlies have a surprising 6-0 record to start the NBA season. Here's why and what it means for their hopes of making the playoffs.
stories.detailText: There's only one undefeated team left in the NBA , and few would have predicted it before the 2026-27 season began . The Memphis Grizzlies are raising eyebrows across the league with a perfect 6-0 record after their front office spent the past 18 months recalibrating the team's roster by trading away Ja Morant , Jaren Jackson Jr. and Desmond Bane . One more victory on Monday, Nov. 2, against the New Orleans Pelicans would set a record for the best start in franchise history. A Grizzlies' nucleus featuring 2026 first-round pick Cameron Boozer, 2025 first-round pick Cedric Coward, 2024 first-round pick Zach Edey and guard Ty Jerome appears capable of exceeding expectations after they were the only team in the league to not have a player included in USA TODAY's top 100 player rankings prior to the season. Six games later, they could be the Western Conference playoff contender nobody expected . During the past 20 seasons, the last remaining undefeated team in the NBA has failed to qualify for the playoffs just three times. No team since the 1998-99 Seattle Supersonics has started a season with at least six wins in a row and not made it to the NBA's postseason. So how have the Grizzlies pulled off this early season surprise? Here are three reasons why Memphis is the last remaining undefeated team in the NBA before games played on Monday, Nov. 2: NBA: Spike Lee hopes Knicks skip Trump White House visit despite Dolan's wishes Cameron Boozer is Grizzlies' next star Yaxel Lendeborg is suddenly the trendy pick to be the NBA's rookie of the year thanks to a batch of big early season performances, but Grizzlies forward Cameron Boozer is the only rookie with a game-winner and a triple-double so far. The No. 3 overall pick in the 2026 NBA Draft has quickly become a hub for the Memphis offense, distributing the ball on offense and forming a fearsome pairing inside with Edey. Though his overall shooting numbers are lagging and he won't wow you with athletic feats, Boozer is still shooting nearly 37% from 3-point range and looks to be a potential cornerstone in the mold of Tim Duncan with his diverse skill set. Perhaps more importantly, his promising production in the first six games have helped shift the narrative after an offseason of uncertainty about the changing roster. Cam Boozer starred in last night's Memphis win! 27 PTS (career-high, 17 in 3Q) 9 REB 26 MIN The Grizzlies are 6-0 for the first time since the 2014-15 NBA season 🔥 pic.twitter.com/1GMWqHQyRp — NBA (@NBA) November 1, 2026 NBA misjudged Grizzlies' depth The Grizzlies might not have a star with the commercial crossover potential Morant once had, but the roster was in much better shape than many NBA prognosticators expected after the team traded away Morant, Jackson, Bane and Santi Aldama in various deals. Memphis currently has 13 players averaging at least 12 minutes per game as coach Tuomas Iisalo often uses an 11-man rotation. Jerome, who missed most of last season after being signed by the Grizzlies, was the league's leading scorer during the first week of the season. Coward and Jaylen Wells have shown growth as 3-point shooters and Edey, despite being on a minutes restriction, has been a dominating rebounder and defensive anchor based on advanced metrics. Jerami Grant and Isaiah Stewart, acquired in trades this past offseason, have provided a veteran presence off a bench that seems to come in waves. That approach might not work in the postseason, and it caused issues when Morant clashed with Iisalo last year. But it's proving effective during the first month of an NBA season that's been defined by the number of injuries impact players have already suffered. Grizzlies' schedule has been soft Memphis has shown undeniable signs that it was overlooked heading into the 2026-27 season and swept a four-game road trip as part of this hot start. But it also hasn't beaten a team expected to contend for either conference title. The Grizzlies have beaten the NBA's only winless team twice (Sacramento Kings) and have two wins over a team with a 1-5 record heading into Monday (Utah Jazz). They'll be favored against the struggling Pelicans. But Memphis also orchestrated a comeback over the Golden State Warriors and handed the Portland Trail Blazers their first loss of the season. Morant played against his former team for the first time in Portland and left with a hamstring injury that will sideline him for at least a month. Six games don't validate a rebuild, and the schedule toughens in the coming weeks. But as Morant faces another extended absence and the Grizzlies keep piling up wins, the franchise's decision to dismantle the roster built around him looks less like a gamble and more like foresight. stories.detailText: Nobody will wear No. 0 for the Oklahoma City Thunder again. The Thunder announced Monday they'll retire Russell Westbrook's jersey on Feb. 7 during a home game against the New York Knicks. General manager Sam Presti made the announcement at Oklahoma City's Day One Luncheon on Monday with Westbrook on stage. Westbrook wiped back tears when the announcement was made. There will be a jersey retirement for Russell Westbrook on Feb 7. pic.twitter.com/2ezwUQy4QD — Addam M. Francisco (@SuaveCEO_) November 2, 2026 The Thunder then released a video montage celebrating Westbrook's moments with the franchise. 0 Forever 💙 02.07.27 pic.twitter.com/pTqRnespU2 — OKC THUNDER (@okcthunder) November 2, 2026 "Many players make an impact but only great players leave a legacy," Presti said, via a team statement . "Russell Westbrook's legacy was built both on the court and in the community." Westbrook's legacy in OKC Westbrook was a member of the Thunder from the beginning. He was drafted by the Seattle SuperSonics with the No. 4 pick in 2008, weeks before the franchise officially moved to Oklahoma City and became the Thunder. Not including previously retired Sonics jerseys, Nick Collison's No. 4 is the only other jersey the Thunder have retired. Westbrook played 11 of his his 18 NBA seasons with the Thunder from 2008-19, including his 2016-17 NBA MVP campaign. He made eight of his nine All-Star teams and earned eight of his nine All-NBA selections with Oklahoma City. Westbrook is the NBA's all-time triple-double king. He became the first player since Oscar Robertson to average a triple-double during his MVP season and did so three more times throughout his career. His 209 triple-doubles are the most all time. Westbrook retired from the NBA in August having also played for the Wizards, Lakers, Clippers, Nuggets and Kings. But he's most closely associated with elevating a Thunder franchise to championship contention alongside Kevin Durant, James Harden and Serge Ibaka. From that core, he remains the most beloved in the Oklahoma City community. Now his jersey will have a permanent place in the Thunder's rafters.

stories.title: ‘Right now a top-10 player’: This NBA insider says it with his chest about Cooper Flagg’s arrival
stories.summary: An ESPN reporter who has covered the Mavericks for years says Cooper Flagg has already arrived in just year two.
stories.detailText: MIAMI, FLORIDA - OCTOBER 26: Cooper Flagg #32 of the Dallas Mavericks drives to the basket against Bam Adebayo #13 of the Miami Heat during the first quarter at Kaseya Center on October 26, 2026 in Miami, Florida. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Megan Briggs/Getty Images) | Getty Images If you’ve been locked in for the Dallas Mavericks’ first six games of the 2026-27 season, you already know. The proof is in the dominance-flavored pudding. And ESPN reporter Tim MacMahon has been. So he knows. That’s why MacMahon had no reservations when he declared flatly on Monday’s episode of the Hoop Collective podcast that Cooper Flagg has already arrived. He’s not going to be one of the best in the league. He is one of the best in the league. Right now. Today. This is no longer something opposing teams can put off until some future point in Flagg’s development. He will wreck your shit tomorrow. The Houston Rockets found out about it in Friday’s first and fourth quarter s of the Mavericks’ 116-111 win at the AAC to improve their record to 4-2. “This is going to get aggregated, and I’m okay with it,” MacMahon said while discussing the Mavericks with podcast host Brian Windhorst, who himself banged a loud drum for Flagg before the start of the season. “I would not trade Cooper Flagg for Luka [Doncic], just considering age, contract, all that kind of stuff. Cooper Flagg I believe right now is a top-10 player.” Then he said it once more, with vigor. “I think he’s a top-10 player. … There’s only one guy in the league I’d trade him for.” I don’t know why there’s a need to commingle this discussion with who one would or wouldn’t trade for Flagg, because the Mavericks ain’t trading Flagg, just as much as the San Antonio Spurs ain’t trading Victor Wembanyama any time soon. Irrelevant. What’s relevant is that Flagg’s development has curved toward the exponential in the tail end of what are still his teen years, which should be a horrifying proposition for the rest of the league, and the Mavericks’ roster is showing signs that the same may be true of the team surrounding the young superstar. Flagg and Kyrie Irving went off for 35 and 33, respectively, in Friday’s upset of the Rockets, who were admittedly playing without Alperen Sengun. MacMahon also stressed on the podcast that it is becoming less and less likely that the team trades Irving this season as the team’s fortunes seem to be turning this year. “Cooper being this good at bringing the ball up and initiating the offense takes a lot of pressure off him and takes a lot of strain off him. Kyrie, I think, is very, very happy and comfortable with his situation in Dallas,” MacMahon said. “My educated guess is that this is probably a situation that plays out this summer, but we’ll see.” Irving has a player option for 2027-28 at just north of $42 million before he becomes an unrestricted free agent after next season. Irving and Flagg work well on the court for the same reason that Irving and Doncic worked, and for the same reason that Irving and LeBron James worked during the Cleveland Cavaliers’ championship season in 2015-16. Having a running partner who can also bring the ball up and initiate offense gives Irving the freedom to play both on and off the ball, maximizing his ability to play-make and get into advantageous matchups for isos. Flagg comes into Monday’s game against the Sacramento Kings averaging 26.8 points per game, which is seventh in the NBA, through six games. He’s also fifth in steals (2.6 per game) and 21st in blocked shots (1.2), making him perhaps the most dominant force on both sides of the ball this side of Wembanyama. And he won’t turn 20 for six more weeks.

stories.title: Late Closeouts, Empty Glass: Breaking Down the NBA’s Worst Defense
stories.summary: The Phoenix Suns’ defense has some work to do.
stories.detailText: Last year, this defense was the whole identity of the team. We watched a roster nobody believed in become a problem every night because they chased, they swiped, they dove on the floor, and they made you earn every bucket. Four games into this season, that team is gone. The Suns are 1-3 and have allowed 122 points or more in all four games. Dillon Brooks stood at the podium and called it what it is: “We’re 30th in defense, so that’s not great. That’s terrible.” Then they spent three days drilling it in practice, came home, and let Denver rain threes in their own building. The fanbase is past the “small sample size” stage. We are watching the same breakdowns repeat. This stat from Cody Hunt on X/Twitter blew my mind. How much is it bad luck? How much is it real? I believe it’s a bit of both, personally. And small sample sizes can blow stats like this out of proportion. But it is clear that this is a massive issue that needs correcting, ASAP. Through 4 games, Suns opponents are shooting 43.9% from 3, which is the highest opponent 3P% in the NBA. 2nd place is at 40.5%, and league average 3P% is 34.6%. How much of that is bad defense vs. just bad luck? — Cody Hunt (@co_dhunt) November 1, 2026 Tactical Breakdown Rotations to shooters are late, every time. Murray and Braun combined for 14 threes, and Brooks and others kept rotating or closing out too late on kick-outs to Braun. Ott pointed out that Braun was “a guy that’s made five all year.” Credit to Braun, but when you leave a shooter wide open, he gets hot. View Link The switching scheme leaves too few defenders on the back side. About a dozen times, the aggressive switching and double-teams on Jokic left one help defender covering two Nuggets on the perimeter. That scheme only works with perfect timing, and right now nobody is in sync. And we saw it snowball. Off-ball attention in the corners. Brooks and Bridges are often stationed in the corner, where they tend to doze off, whether that means losing a backdoor cutter, reacting late, or failing to rebound. Booker’s league-worst 137.2 individual defensive rating gets the headlines, but the leaks are coming from every spot on the floor. Again, the problem I have with all of this is that they had a full three days to talk about this and work on it. And while they looked much sharper offensively (outside of Jalen Green), the defense stuck out like a sore thumb yet again. Team huddle. Dillon Brooks, Collin Gillespie, Jordan Ott and Suns assistants Brian Randle and John Little talking after Wednesday's practice. Brooks said they talked about defense and as he called it "terrible" so far this season. #Suns pic.twitter.com/EH6AKZZOod — Duane Rankin (@DuaneRankin) October 28, 2026 The Size/Athleticism Filter This roster was built to be long and nasty, and the length is not showing up where it matters. At 27.7 defensive rebounds per game, only Golden State has been worse at ending opponent possessions. With Mark Williams out and Oso Ighodaro missing a couple of games, the frontcourt has been thin and young, and Khaman Maluach is taking on a big role early. Ott explained the trade-off himself: the team is “so concerned on the glass” that players retreat to rebound instead of pressuring the ball, and without stops they end up inbounding after made baskets. Last year the athleticism produced steals and transition buckets. This year it is being spent cleaning up misses that should have been contested in the first place. The defense was the engine for everything else. The Suns ranked third in steals last season, and that pressure is what made the chaos offense work. Without it, this is a half-court team with spacing problems. The front line defense is vital not only for containing penetration that leads to clean looks, but also for stopping guys like Jamal Murray from going supernova and dropping 39 with ease, which I talked about in my latest episode of Suns Hit . The lineup questions are already here. Jalen Green’s defensive rating sits at 130.7, while Collin Gillespie’s is 120.3, and Ott went with Gillespie next to Booker down the stretch instead of Green. They will need the defense to step up against a Warriors team that can shoot the basketball well from deep. They hunt three-point looks. And have some guy named Stephen Curry who is pretty good at shooting the basketball. Golden State drilled 22 threes on 45% shooting in a win over the Clippers on Sunday night, and have won 4 straight games since their loss to the Suns. That decision (starters) is going to get louder every week the defense stays at the bottom of the league. The lone cure to that is winning, and even that may be a band-aid if they can’t figure out how to make this group work long-term. Closing Thought The talk is already done. The film is there. Close out on shooters. Box out the man in your area. Defense should be the priority. If the Booker-Green-Brooks-Bridges core can’t defend together, Ott has to stop forcing it and play the lineups that get stops. Last year’s top-10 defense came from effort and execution, and right now this team has neither. For the 10th time in their first 15 quarters this season, the Phoenix Suns have surrendered 30+ points. That’s 67% of the quarters they’ve played. At some point, this stops being an occasional defensive breakdown and starts becoming your defensive identity. https://t.co/SIp046iqDu — John Voita, III (@DarthVoita) October 31, 2026

In speaking with reporters prior to Sunday’s win over the Toronto Raptors , head coach JJ Redick didn’t seem too worried about Williams’ status, however. “The images have been clean. It’s this, I would describe it as a soreness that just pops up in the morning,” Redick said. “He’s feeling a lot better. I think just being, again, cautious with the back to back.” Los Angeles has gone 2-1 without Williams in the lineup as Jake LaRavia’s stepped up to replace his sidelined teammate. In Williams’ stead, LaRavia is averaging 6.7 points (46.7% shooting, 50% from deep), 4.7 rebounds, 1.7 steals, 1.3 blocks and 1.3 assists over the past three outings. Before injury struck, Williams was filling a crucial role for the Lakers as one of their primary point-of-attack stoppers and an efficient off-ball scorer capitalizing on his chances alongside Luka Dončić and Austin Reaves. In four games, he’s averaging a career-high 11.3 points (69.2% on 2-pointers, 46.7% beyond the arc), 3.0 rebounds, 2.3 assists and 1.5 steals. Los Angeles has outscored its opponents by 29 points during his 114 minutes this season. Already fairly thin on the wing, especially at power forward, the Lakers will hope Williams is back sooner rather than later. Aside from Monday’s second leg of a back-to-back, they don’t have another back-to-back until Nov. 17 and 18, so the schedule isn’t too jumbled in the coming weeks. That should help limit how many — if any — more games Williams misses. Courtesy of another sensational performance on Sunday from Dončić (45 points, 15 rebounds, six assists, five steals, one block), the Lakers dispatched the Kawhi Leonard-less Raptors, 131-125, and moved to 5-2, good for fourth in the West (if an early season standings watch is your cup of tea). stories.title: The Lakers 'live on a spaceship,' and Luka Dončić looks like the best damn pilot in the galaxy
stories.summary: The All-NBA playmaker has started the season on the kind of offensive heater that has the Lakers dreaming big.
stories.detailText: Perhaps, while watching him flame-broil the Toronto Raptors on Sunday night to the tune of 45 points on 12-for-23 shooting with eight 3-pointers, you found yourself thinking, "Man, Luka Dončić is on an all-time heater to start the season." Well, if it seems that way, it's because he very, very much is: Luka Dončić (226) becomes the third player in NBA history since 1960 to tally 225+ points through his first six games of a season, joining Michael Jordan (1986) and Wilt Chamberlain (2x) 😳 https://t.co/Y2bo9xWcyw pic.twitter.com/k15DP61Qie — NBA History (@NBAHistory) November 2, 2026 "You need three guys to guard him," Lakers big man Sandro Mamukelashvili said, according to ESPN . "I have a feeling that every time Luka plays, it's like 35-plus [points]." Pretty close, Mamu. It's actually four times in six games this season. (The last four, if you're keeping score.) Much of the postgame commentary about Dončić's performance in the Los Angeles Lakers' 131-125 win over the Raptors focused on his defensive work : on the 15 defensive rebounds he pulled down, on the five steals he snagged and six deflections he piled up, on the charges he took to draw offensive fouls and get the Lakers another possession. That certainly matters; Dončić is no stranger to catching hell for lacking defensive effort on the sport's grandest stage , and these Lakers will need him to put his best foot forward on that end if they hope to get back to that stage themselves. "We've been relying on our offense a lot," Lakers center Walker Kessler told reporters after a loss to the Portland Trail Blazers last week. "And we have a very, very good offense and a lot of great scorers. But that's not gonna be the only thing that gets us to win a championship here." It won't. It'll be the main thing, though. Because what the Lakers did, after ending the somewhat awkward stuck-between-stations stint that stretched from Dončić's arrival at the 2025 trade deadline and the team bidding farewell to LeBron James this summer, was build A Luka Dončić Team. And if there's one thing A Luka Dončić Team is going to do, it's score a truckload of points — with the lion's share of them coming off the fingertips of No. 77. Sunday's monstrous performance against the Raptors made Dončić just the second player since the NBA began tracking steals in 1973 to score 45 points, collect 15 rebounds, dish 5 assists and grab 5 steals in a single game — joining, as luck would have it, Anthony Davis , the man whom the Lakers traded to Dallas to secure Dončić's services nearly two years ago. It was his 24th career 45-point game , tying George Gervin for 10th on the all-time list, and his 11th career 45-point, 10-rebound, 5-assist outing — more than anybody but Laker legends Wilt Chamberlain and Elgin Baylor. Six times, Dončić has suited up for the Lakers this season; three times, he's topped 40 points. He is now averaging more than one point per minute — a historical rate of offensive onslaught that nobody has surpassed since Wilt did it 65 years ago . This isn't normal. Luka just makes it seem that way. "It feels like a supernova, but it also feels normal," Lakers head coach JJ Redick told reporters after Sunday's win. "We live on a spaceship and we're going at the speed of light at all times when he's on the court." Dončić has opened the season looking like the best damn pilot in the galaxy, leading the NBA in scoring at 37.7 points per game, 8.1 points more than second-place Tyrese Maxey. That 8.1-point gap between first and second place is roughly the same as the gap between Maxey and Indiana Pacers forward Pascal Siakam, whose 21.4 points per game rank 28th in the NBA. Dončić leads the NBA in made field goals per game, in 3-pointers made and attempted per game and in free throws made and attempted per game. He's converting on all those looks at or near career-best rates , shooting 78% at the rim, 53% from floater range, 47% on long-2 midrange looks, 90% from the free-throw line, and 43.2% from long distance. He's also tied for ninth in the NBA in assists, dishing 7.3 dimes per contest, making him one of two players in the top 10 in both categories, alongside Jayson Tatum of the Boston Celtics. Combine the points that Dončić is generating by setting up his big men at the rim and shooters on the perimeter with the ones that he's scoring himself, and he's creating 55.3 points of offense for the Lakers per game — most in the NBA, according to Databallr . Including plays where he shoots or passes to a teammate who shoots, Dončić's pick-and-rolls are producing 1.18 points per play, the third-highest mark among players who've run at least 50 pick-and-rolls, according to Synergy Sports Technology's tracking. His isolations are generating 1.22 points per possession — fifth-best among players who've finished at least 20 one-on-one trips. When he orchestrates from the post, the Lakers have scored 1.36 points per trip — fourth-most among players to log at least 10 such plays. Add it all up, and the Los Angeles offense has been an absolute buzzsaw with Luka at the controls. The Lakers have scored a scorching 130.7 points per 100 non-garbage-time possessions in Dončić's minutes ; as a point of comparison, the league-leading Rockets offense averages 122.1 . They're shooting the cover off the ball from everywhere with him on the floor : 80% at the rim, 58% from midrange and 43% from 3-point land. They've been elite in the half-court , with Dončić poking and prodding and bending coverages until they snap. They've been even better in transition , where Dončić's combination of excellent defensive rebounding for a wing and perpetual eyes-up scanning for hit-ahead opportunities allow L.A. to get out and run into easy buckets: "When he has it going, it's like, pick your poison, cause he can just make any shot," Redick said. "And then you start putting two on the ball, and everybody else is the beneficiary of that. He's a terrific offensive engine." That engine is running red-hot to start the season, pacing the Lakers to a 5-2 record behind the NBA's No. 3 offense , with Dončić playing like an MVP frontrunner — and getting the help he needs from the Lakers' other core pieces. Second banana Austin Reaves is averaging 23 points and five assists per game on 52/40/88 shooting. New center Kessler is holding up his end of the bargain, shooting a league-best 75.4% from the field, averaging 10 rebounds and 3 blocks per game, and holding opponents to a microscopic 41.3% at the rim when he's the closest defender; that's the best mark of any interior deterrent to face at least 25 up-close shots, according to Second Spectrum tracking . All told, the Lakers have blitzed opponents by 84 points in 126 minutes with Dončić, Reaves and Kessler on the court together — the best point differential of any three-man unit in the league thus far — and their core lineups have largely been lights out, with a number of role players (Mamukelashvili, Ziaire Williams, Matisse Thybulle, et al.) providing the right kind of production and filling in the gaps around that high-priced, high-wattage core. The spaceship could hit some turbulence, though. The Lakers have played one of the league's easier schedules thus far; three of their five wins have come against the Clippers and Jazz. They're also outperforming their expected field goal percentage to a higher degree than any other team in the league, according to multiple shot-quality metrics . If that red-hot collective shooting normalizes — and if the ball-security issues that have L.A. ranking 28th in team turnover percentage , with Dončić and Reaves sitting first and second in the league in total cough-ups — then the Lakers could be in for some regression … especially if, y'know, Luka doesn't continue to average like 38 points per game on Prime Steph shooting and Prime Harden usage for a full season. Of note: Luka's never gotten to the basket less. His 18 drives per game are the third - lowest average since entering the NBA, and a career-low 9% of his shot attempts have come at the rim, according to Cleaning the Glass . He's balanced that out by taking more than half of his attempts from 3-point land for the first time in his career, which is a pretty good idea when you're making them; what happens, though, if those stepbacks aren't cashing in at a 43% clip? If and when that comes, some of those other shortcomings — the hole at power forward, the lack of another viable ball-handler to help Reaves buoy the offense when Dončić rests, the worrisome lack of rebounding and interior heft when Kessler's off the floor, etc. — could become more glaring. For now, though, the Lakers are off to what's been by and large a glass-half-full start: a top-three offense with a just-below-average defense , outscoring opponents by 7.5 points-per-100 (a 58-win pace ), with Dončić looking like the best player on the floor damn near every time he sets foot on it, somehow making the obscene look routine. It doesn't seem possible that a spaceship like these Lakers can keep going at the speed of light without eventually slowing down. That's the thing about superstars like Dončić, though: When they've got it going, the limits of physics and history and even our imaginations can just seem to fade away. "All of the great, great players that have ever played have also been in the 1% competitor [level]," Lakers assistant coach Greg St. Jean recently told Thuc Nhi Nguyen of the Los Angeles Times . "They've always been the guy that is able to inspire the players around him and be able to do things that don't even seem like they're possible. And he does that nightly."

stories.title: Spike Lee hopes Knicks skip Trump White House visit despite Dolan's wishes
stories.summary: Spike Lee made his stance clear on a potential White House visit for the defending NBA champion New York Knicks in a new interview.
stories.detailText: The New York Knicks' most famous fan is urging the team to skip a White House visit. Spike Lee told Variety in an interview published Monday that he hopes the Knicks decline an invitation to celebrate their 2026 NBA championship with President Donald Trump amid reports of disagreement within the organization over a potential visit. ESPN's Stephen A. Smith said last week that owner James Dolan was unhappy with players over their apparent reluctance to make the trip. Dolan is a major Trump donor and longtime friend who hosted the U.S. President in his suite at Madison Square Garden for Game 3 of the 2026 NBA Finals. NBA CUP: 2026 schedule, format, groups and more "He can’t force them!" Lee said when asked about the apparent rift between Dolan and the players over a potential White House visit. "It’s been years since the last NBA team has gone. They’re not going. I hope they don’t go! I hope they don’t go." Dolan notably gave $125,000 to Trump's re-election campaign efforts in 2017, according to multiple reports, five days after Trump's public spat with the then-NBA champion Golden State Warriors about whether Stephen Curry had declined an invite to the White House or Trump rescinded the invitation. No NBA champion has visited the White House during either of Trump's terms in office as U.S. President. The Oklahoma City Thunder did not visit the White House last year following their 2025 NBA title due to a "timing issue." The 2024 champion Boston Celtics, meanwhile, did visit former President Joe Biden at the White House to celebrate their title in November 2024. The Denver Nuggets did not celebrate at the White House due to scheduling issues on Biden's end , while the Milwaukee Bucks and Warriors each had customary White House visits under the Biden administration in 2021 and 2022. Prior to the Bucks, the Cleveland Cavaliers had been the last team to visit the White House in 2016 when former President Barack Obama was still in office. Knicks star Jalen Brunson previously said in July the team had not yet discussed whether to celebrate their title at the White House and pushed back on assumptions that a decision had already been made. His comments came after Dolan had said in a radio interview that the franchise had already accepted an invitation to visit the White House. Lee told Variety that many New York Yankees fans disagreed with former owner George Steinbrenner's Republican politics, but argued Steinbrenner never brought politicians to the games. Lee believes Trump's attendance at Game 3 of the NBA Finals may have disrupted the Knicks' momentum. The game was New York's lone loss of the series. "That was not just an accident!" Lee said. Lee also suggested Dolan picked Ben Stiller over him, to produce a documentary that Stiller was seen filming from his courtside seats during the Knicks' NBA Finals run. "It was Dolan. Dolan gave it to him," Lee said. "Look, it’s his team, he can do what he wants to do. Coulda woulda, but it’s his team. He also wants his team to go to the White House, too." This article originally appeared on USA TODAY: Spike Lee hopes Knicks skip Trump White House visit despite Dolan's wishes

stories.title: Lakers’ JJ Redick exposes NBA’s officiating flaw after win over Raptors
stories.summary: Lakers coach JJ Redick is tired of fouls not being called.
stories.detailText: When it came to officiating the Raptors’ aggressive perimeter defense, Sunday night went exactly as JJ Redick described it would. Before his team’s victory over the Raptors at Crypto.com Arena , the Lakers coach was asked whether there’s anything the Raptors do tactically to be as proficient with forcing turnovers as they are. Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick wasn’t happy with how the Raptors defense had been officiated on Sunday. AP Photo/Scott Strazzante The Raptors entered Sunday ranked No. 1 in turnovers forced and defensive turnover percentage, but also committed the most personal fouls per game. “If you look at the team – and this is not like a shot, this is just reality – a lot of the teams that force turnovers, they foul a lot,” Redick said. “And so by fouling on every possession, the refs are just naturally gonna allow you leeway. “Oklahoma City does that. Detroit, watching this team, this version of this Raptors team on film, they remind me a lot of like last year’s Detroit team where they’re just going to foul you on every possession. And obviously they’ve also been called for the most fouls, and they’ve given up the most free throws, so that’s part of it.” Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick sees flaws in how NBA officials referee teams with aggressive perimeter defenders. NBAE via Getty Images The game played as Redick said it would. The Lakers finished with 24 turnovers that directly resulted in 30 points for the Raptors, who also committed 26 personal fouls. While taking care of the ball has been a struggle for the Lakers, Redick saw what happened Sunday as a reflection of how NBA officials referee games in the modern era. “I mean you guys can see it – some of those turnovers are because we’re legitimately getting fouled,” Redick said. “I told one of the referees this ‘cause all these guys do it, all the on ball defenders [do it] now. What they do is they pick you up and then they grab the arm you’re not dribbling with and then they try to steal the ball from you. “Famously Cason Wallace did it with TJ McConnell [in Game 7 of the 2025 NBA finals]. And that’s just the NBA right now. “It’s really hard when you play teams like this that are just fouling every possession. We did enough to play through it. But a lot of those turnovers are just that and then you can point to some decision making [with] some passes, all that stuff. Those naturally happen within the flow of the game.” The Lakers aren’t shy with their issues with officials. Getty Images Lakers superstar Luka Dončić, who’s often being guarded by the team’s best defenders, has noticed the shift in how perimeter defenders are officiated over the last couple of years. “In the last two years, the game has become way more physical,” Dončić said. “They allow way more contact. But obviously like you said, the refs can’t call everything. We just need to learn from them. We need to do the same things. Use that on the defensive end. You got to use aggression towards them. We just got to learn from that and we should do all the same on defense.”

stories.detailText: Golden State Warriors Yaxel Lendeborg discusses his performance against the Clippers. In Sunday’s 124-112 victory against the Los Angeles Clippers, Golden State Warriors rookie phenom Yaxel Lendeborg fell just shy of scoring 40 points. It is the most for a Warriors rookie since Stephen Curry in 2010. Lendeborg finished with 37 points and was asked why he didn’t go for the 40-point figure. He indeed tried, but fell short because of the pressure from his peers. Yaxel Lendeborg considers himself an "ethical hooper" pic.twitter.com/ZNiMtJCxjx — Warriors on NBCS (@NBCSWarriors) November 2, 2026 Yaxel Lendeborg scores 37 points in Sunday’s game against the Los Angeles Clippers. NBAE via Getty Images “I’ve never been a stat chaser in my life, so just falling into peer pressure like I did just now was pretty much bad on my part,” Lendeborg said. “Especially because I’m a guy that just loves ethical hoops. I’m a guy that loves efficient basketball, and I didn’t do that the last two or three minutes. So it’s kind of bad on my part.” Lendeborg said his teammate De’Anthony Melton approached him and said , “Hey man you need to get 40. You’re three points away.’ And I’m like, ‘Nah, man. It’s all good.’ And he peer pressured me into doing it.” Yaxel Lendeborg celebrating with Will Richard during his 37 point performance on Sunday night. NBAE via Getty Images “He said he’s going to give me the ball. And he literally like, was holding it just to give me the ball. And I’m like, ‘All right, fine. I’ll shoot it.’ And I missed.” Lendeborg said he tried to barter with Melton about being content with his 37 points, but then Will Richard approached him and said, “You got to do it.” “Everybody was just egging me on, and I kind of just fell into it. But I know next time, I’mma just play in the flow of the game, ’cause they came out of me like four threes in a row, and we almost lost the game because of that. So, next time I’m never doing that again.” It is not often you hear a professional athlete openly talk about trying to pad their stats. Yet, the Warriors rookie is not one for holding back. Golden State Warriors rookie, Yaxel Lendeborg scores 37 points against the Clippers on Sunday night. Getty Images “If it comes to me, it does. If I don’t get it, then I wasn’t meant to get it that day,” Lendeborg said. “Imma be way better next time.” Steve Kerr told reporters he’s enjoyed watching his rookie shine, saying, “he’s playing this way and he really doesn’t know the NBA game yet. …He’s going to get a lot better.”

stories.detailText: The NBA is only a few games deep, but leaguewide buzz never stops. The LeBron James and Jaylen Brown era with the Philadelphia 76ers got off to an ideal start by spoiling ring night for the New York Knicks . The Detroit Pistons also returned to their regular-season dominance with a win over the Boston Celtics , and the Oklahoma City Thunder struck the first rivalry blow against the San Antonio Spurs this season. Now, what will Giannis Antetokounmpo 's first season away from Milwaukee look like? And how will the other new faces in new places make their impact this season? All season, bookmark this page for the latest news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders. Quick links: Free agency grades | Trade grades Trade tracker | Transactions | Offseason buzz Depth charts | Trade machine | More Nov. 2 Hoop Collective: Is Houston an NBA Finals sleeper? And 76ers' dream start Brian is joined by ESPN's Tim MacMahon to discuss the Houston Rockets ' 6-1 start and whether they are a legitimate title contender. Also, just as much as he means to that locker room and as well as he's working with Cooper [Flagg], it was beautiful basketball. "And just basketball wise they are a phenomenal fit. And I do think there's a legitimate argument to be made for the value of playing meaningful games in March and April for the development of a superstar like Cooper, of young role players like Zaccharie Risacher , who, by the way, is doing some really interesting things -- on the defensive end especially -- and he's got a player option next year. "I think it's a situation where you can get together and handle it in the summer. It's not like you have to either move them or lose them, by this deadline." Nembhard, 23, played 60 games (27 starts) for the Dallas Mavericks in 2025-26 after signing as an undrafted free agent. He was traded to the Atlanta Hawks then to the Charlotte Hornets this offseason before being waived. Sept. 29 Charania: NBA reviewing finalists' bids for Vegas team ESPN's Shams Charania reported that the NBA is currently reviewing finalist bids for a new expansion team in Las Vegas. The price range is currently speculated at $12-13 billion with a new arena factored into the cost. The three final groups are Nancy Walton Laurie and Bill Laurie; Steve Apostolopoulos and Marc Lasry; Bill Foley and Jerry Colangelo, sources told ESPN. Will KAT take a pay cut in next Knicks deal? On "NBA Today," ESPN's Malika Andrews detailed Karl-Anthony Towns ' mindset toward contract negotiations with the defending champion New York Knicks . "Towns, from what I have been told, is willing -- similarly to what Jalen Brunson did [but the] numbers aren't the same -- to take a pay cut," Andrews said. "But the pay cut that the Knicks are asking him to take, he views as unreasonable." Towns, 30, is eligible to sign a four-year, $276 million extension through June 30. Embiid "full participant" in first Sixers' practice Joel Embiid was a "full participant all the way through" for the Philadelphia 76ers first practice of training camp, Sixers coach Nick Nurse said Tuesday. "He looked great," Nurse said of Embiid. "Very, very good news from the standpoint of where it's been the last couple years, last couple summers leading into today. ... It's great to see." After being named the league MVP in 2023, the 32-year-old center has missed 150 games over the last three seasons because of various injuries. He also sat out four of the Sixers' 11 playoff games in the spring because of appendicitis, right hip soreness and a right ankle sprain. The only Sixers player who did not participate in Tuesday's practice according to a team spokesperson was backup big man Adem Bona , who is dealing with a sprained left foot. Anfernee Simons , who signed a two-year, $12.3 million contract to join Philadelphia in July, said Embiid's presence in the gym was already notable leading up to the start of camp. "Everybody's been impressed around here about how he's come in and worked," Simons said. "Joel is going to be Joel. He's going to be a dominant player always. We just want to continue for him to be himself, as well, and I think everybody's going to be able to work around that." Despite the injuries, the 10-year veteran still averaged 26.9 points, 7.7 rebounds, 3.9 assists and 1.2 blocks per game last season. Embiid's inclusion only added to what several Sixers players described as an "exciting" opening day with LeBron James and Jaylen Brown completing their first official practice with the franchise. "With any team, we got to start somewhere, and then we got to get better and better, and just keep trying to reach our ceiling, right?" Nurse said. "That happens day-to-day. Can we get up tomorrow, like, 98% as excited as we did today? It's going to be hard to get as excited as we all were today, right? "But we need to come back, and we need to keep climbing that mountain. That's a daily process. I just want them to reach their potential. If they do, great things are going to happen." -- Dave McMenamin Hoop Collective: The 2026 NBA Media Day reaction special Brian Windhorst is joined by ESPN reporters from around the league to check in on Monday's Media Days. But when it came to his son/teammate Bronny, much was apparently left unsaid . "We're men of very little words when it comes to talking about business and what we're going to do and how we feel about each other. LeBron and Bronny have routinely been in unique situations in league history, whether it was opening night two years ago, when the father and son entered the game together, or last year in the playoffs, where they combined to deliver a 10-0 run during a victory over the Houston Rockets . Navigating a complex free agency in which the father leaves and the son stays is another one for the books. Tatum 'comfortable' leading new-look Celtics post-Brown trade Jayson Tatum 's one constant during his development into a star with the Boston Celtics was having Jaylen Brown as a teammate. That partnership ended this offseason when the Celtics' front office decided to trade Brown -- the 2024 NBA Finals MVP -- to the Philadelphia 76ers in what was largely a cost-cutting move that broke up the duo most responsible for leading Boston to the 2024 NBA championship. "The business of the NBA comes and plays a part at some point. And I've seen it in my almost 10 years in this league," Tatum said during Celtics media day on Monday . "For me it's more so being grateful for what we accomplished and what he means for this city and to this organization. Just the ups and downs in our career that we were able to grow and learn from and made us the players that we are today. So really just being thankful for those nine years." Suns owner Ishbia says mortgage company woes won't hurt team It's well-known at this point that billionaire Mat Ishbia's mortgage company has had a rough financial stretch. The owner of the Phoenix Suns said Monday that will have "zero" effect on his spending habits when it comes to basketball. In fact, the 46-year-old said he's working on purchasing 14% more of the team, bringing his total to roughly 80%. Ishbia's company -- United Wholesale Mortgage -- suffered a reported $450 million net loss in the second quarter this year, calling into question if the sizable dip would affect his basketball business. The outspoken Ishbia was adamant that nothing would change for the NBA franchise when it comes to spending on players or the fan experience. Williamson not where he wants to be New Orleans Pelicans forward Zion Williamson kept his answer brief when asked how he would summarize his first seven years as an NBA player. "I'm not where I want to be," said Williamson, whom the Pelicans drafted with the No. 1 pick out of Duke in 2019. "I'm not where I need to be." Butler indicates he is 'ahead' in his knee rehab Nearing the eight-month mark since his right ACL surgery , Jimmy Butler III is hesitant to put a specific target date on his eventual NBA return, but he did express optimism in advance of Golden State Warriors training camp. "I promise you I'm coming back, and it's going to be -- I think it's going to be, like, real eye-popping for everybody how I'm still going to be nice," Butler said. "Probably nicer, honestly." Butler has only recently advanced to running, and he will be limited to light on-court individual work when the team begins practice in Hawaii on Tuesday afternoon. It will be several weeks before Butler is expected to advance to a more rigorous stage of his rehab, and the team's lead medical decision-maker, Rick Celebrini, is known for his cautiousness in the later stages of the rehab process. A January or February return can be considered on the optimistic side for Butler, who turned 37 earlier this month. But Butler did say that the strengthening tests on the knee indicate he is ahead of schedule. "My numbers are staggering," Butler said. "They're off the charts. I'm ahead, so they say. So, I just know that all the work that I've been doing, whether it be at home, in L.A., in Europe, in South America, wherever the case may be, I've been doing all the right things. So, I am confident that whenever I come back, I'll be more than ready, I'll be more than healthy and I'll be a better all-around player than I was whenever I went down." -- Anthony Slater Pistons eye "better version" of Cunningham Detroit Pistons coach J.B. Bickerstaff has held many offseason conversations with All-NBA guard Cade Cunningham about seizing greatness and the necessary steps toward improving after last year's playoff run that stretched to Game 7 of the Eastern Conference semifinals. Bickerstaff has guaranteed "a better version" Cunningham this season, which could be a scary sight after he averaged 23.9 points, 9.9 assists, 5.5 rebounds and 1.4 steals in 33.9 minutes during 2025-26. But Cunningham also led the East in turnovers per game after finishing with the second most in 2024-25. "I don't have to challenge Cade, and that's why he is who he is," Bickerstaff said. "Because he's pulling. He's not being pushed." Cunningham showed up in a fresh pair of Nike S.T. Charge "Detroit Tough" sneakers in Pistons colors. He will also receive his own signature Nike shoe, which is expected to debut during the second half of the season. "I'm thankful to be in these shoes. I'm thankful to have the opportunity to represent my family in this way," Cunningham said. "Represent where I come from, but then to represent the city of Detroit. "In a city like this, it's a blessing. I'm thankful for it, I don't take it for granted and I'm trying to make the most out of it." -- Eric Woodyard Hornets waive former No. 8 pick Dillingham The Charlotte Hornets are waiving guard Rob Dillingham , sources told ESPN's Shams Charania . Dillingham was traded from the Chicago Bulls on Saturday for Buddy Hield and cash. The Hornets created a $9.6 million trade exception with the move. Dillingham, 21, appeared in 30 games for the Bulls last season, averaging 9.6 points and 2.8 assists. SGA on chance at historic third straight MVP At Oklahoma City Thunder media day, guard Shai Gilgeous-Alexander discussed the possibility of winning a third straight NBA MVP award and whether that's something he ponders going into this season. "No different than any other year: Try to be the best player I can be, try to implement the things I just worked on," Gilgeous-Alexander said. "The decision for MVP is literally 82 games away. I'm not going to win the award in the first week of the season. ... That kind of recipe for me in the past has kind of worked, and I've been fortunate to win two in a row. "We need to be laser focused on ourselves. We need to take the lessons from that [Western Conference finals] series, for sure, and we did. But it's certainly not something that we overcorrect for, because you end up chasing your shadow, and it prevents you from being your best as you move forward." ESPN's Summer Forecast gave Gilgeous-Alexander the fourth-best chance at the 2027 MVP, behind Victor Wembanyama , Nikola Jokic and Luka Doncic . No player has won three consecutive MVPs since Larry Bird in 1984, 1985 and 1986. -- Baxter Holmes Doncic talks LeBron exit, Lakers "championship" ceiling Speaking to ESPN's Brian Windhorst during Los Angeles Lakers media day, guard Luka Doncic detailed his reaction to LeBron James leaving for the Philadelphia 76ers this past summer and why he thinks a successful 2026-27 includes a Lakers run to the title: "It was kind of sad. Playing with LeBron was amazing. There's a lot of things I learned from him. ... We all know who LeBron James is." Shams: Duren's relationship with Pistons "has fractures" Simmons "didn't touch a ball for a year" During Sacramento Kings media day, guard Ben Simmons laid out the reasons he chose the Kings and why he's excited for the 2026-27 season. "The expectations are low. I feel like that's been something on me too, so we can relate in that way," Simmons told reporters. "I think we have a chip on our shoulder." Simmons last played in 2024-25, appearing in 51 games for the Brooklyn Nets and LA Clippers . The three-time All-Star said the time away gave him the chance to focus on "getting my body right and my mind right." Pistons GM hasn't spoken with Duren all summer Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have a decision to make as the clock ticks closer to Oct. 1 -- the deadline to sign a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer. For Duren, he can accept the five-year, $200 million contract that has been offered by Detroit or he can become the first player named All-NBA or All-Star to sign the qualifying offer. If he chooses the latter, Duren will hold veto power on any trade this season and be an unrestricted free agent next summer. For the Pistons, weighing the risk of having an All-NBA player on a one-year contract and, more importantly, the likelihood he will depart next summer as a free agent is key. There are eight projected teams that have significant cap space to sign Duren to a four-year, $189 million max contract. "I can't control the different things that he does or his group does," Pistons president of basketball operations Trajan Langdon said at media day. "For me, it's control what we can and letting him know he is a big part of what we do." Langdon also said he hasn't spoken with Duren all summer during Pistons media day. -- Bobby Marks Mitchell: LeBron to Cavs made sense "for a lot of reasons" At Cavaliers media day, Donovan Mitchell said that in his mind, he thought LeBron James would return to Cleveland because "for a lot of reasons it made sense." "I didn't think Philly. I thought if he didn't come here, it'd be Golden State," Mitchell said. After being swept in the Eastern Conference finals by the eventual champion New York Knicks then missing out on James in free agency, Cleveland kept its core intact. The Cavs signed Mitchell to a four-year, $273 million maximum extension and re-signed James Harden to a three-year, $97 million contract. Cleveland did make one major addition by acquiring Peyton Watson from the Denver Nuggets in a multiteam trade then signing the restricted free agent to a four-year, $88 million deal. Speaking for the first time since their extensions, Mitchell and Harden both said their approaches to their new deals -- Mitchell signing as soon as he was eligible with Harden opting out to give Cleveland more flexibility to make moves -- reflected a team-first mindset. "This is something that I want to do, and I want to win a championship," Harden said. "So, what does that look like? Making the team better, making the team whole to where we give ourselves a chance. By the way, you can have the best talented team, which I've been on before, and still not win. "We waited, waited, waited until the front office called me, made sure that we got everything that we can get, and then we signed. We got a long way to go, but I love the direction and steps that we're taking here as a unit from top to bottom." -- Daniel Oyefusi MacMahon: Thunder adjusting to roster changes The departures of three championship-winning teammates doesn't yet feel like reality for Thunder superstar Shai Gilgeous-Alexander , who kidded that he still expected Luguentz Dort , Isaiah Joe and Aaron Wiggins to show up for Oklahoma City's team picture Monday afternoon. "It's the business of the NBA, right?" Gilgeous-Alexander said, referring to the series of financially motivated trades. "I don't think anybody has played with all 12 guys their whole career. It sucks a little bit. "My mind never even went to what we were going to be like on the court. It was more like the brotherhood." As fellow OKC guard Jalen Williams added, "It's the weirdest thing ever." -- Tim MacMahon Clippers announce Ingram has partially torn Achilles The LA Clippers announced they found a partially torn Achilles tendon in Brandon Ingram 's foot after his recent heel surgery. He will miss the start of the 2026-27 season. Jokic: "I'm gonna sign next year" Denver Nuggets center Nikola Jokic reiterated his commitment to the franchise at Monday's media day. "I'm gonna sign next year," Jokic said. "If they want me." Curry said knee is ready to go for the season Golden State Warriors superstar guard Stephen Curry addressed the media Monday in offering positive updates on his injured knee. "Knee's feeling great. Ready to go. No issues," Curry said. "I feel a lot stronger and understanding of what I'm dealing with." Curry did acknowledge a "management element" but said there are currently no restrictions. Nuggets confident in Jokic's future with franchise Members of the Denver Nuggets ' front office, general manager Jon Wallace and executive vice president of basketball Ben Tenzer addressed the media on Monday and answered questions regarding Nikola Jokic 's future with the franchise. The three-time MVP didn't sign an extension this offseason. "We feel very comfortable with the relation and trust there," Tenzer said. "We have no concerns." LeBron: I wanted to finish my career with the Knicks New Philadelphia 76er LeBron James said his decision came down to five teams this offseason and that he envisioned going to the New York Knicks before they won the 2026 title. "I had visions of playing in [Madison Square] Garden and finishing my career in the Garden," James told ESPN on Monday during the 76ers' media day. "One of the best places I've ever played. "I think it's the No. 1 arena in the world, as far as for a basketball player. But after they beat San Antonio, I was like, 'Hey, I can't.' I couldn't do it." No update on Gary Trent Jr. investigation Milwaukee Bucks governor Wes Edens did not provide an update on the league investigation into Gary Trent Jr. 's contract. "I don't have any update," Edens said. "We're working with the league and fully cooperating with them. But I don't have any insight beyond that." The NBA is looking into a potential cap-circumvention violation by the Bucks around Trent's deal this offseason. Cronin: Blazers have "belief" in Ja Morant Portland Trail Blazers ' general manager Joe Cronin addressed why the franchise decided to trade for Ja Morant this offseason during Portland's media day on Monday. "Just straight belief in Ja," Cronin said. "Our view of Ja as still a very high-level player. "I'm sure there will be questions about fit, but we're very focused on talent." Cronin also said veteran guard Jrue Holiday could play some minutes on the wing for Portland this season, while adding that Holiday and veteran guard Damian Lillard will have a positive influence on Morant. Kerr: Rookie Lendeborg going to "play a ton" Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said during Monday's media day that he expects rookie Yaxel Lendeborg to "play a ton" this season. "He's clearly going to play a ton," Kerr said. "He gives us the size and the versatility that we need. "Whether he's a starter or coming off the bench, that will be determined the next couple of weeks." Lendeborg was the No. 11 pick in the 2026 NBA draft and averaged 15.1 points per game at Michigan last season. Embiid: 'Extremely excited' about this year's team Philadelphia 76ers center Joel Embiid said Monday that he feels like the team finally has the right mix of players, after an offseason in which the franchise traded for Jaylen Brown and signed LeBron James to join the young guard tandem of VJ Edgecombe and Tyrese Maxey . "It's hard to win when you get a group of guys together for one year, two years, maybe," he said. "I'm extremely excited about this team because we have the right mix of veteran leadership and younger guys. We might have some ups and downs, but we're gonna get there." Wembanyama addresses last year's Finals loss After leading by double digits in each of the five games in last season's NBA Finals, San Antonio Spurs center Victor Wembanyama said his memories of it will fuel the team this season. "I couldn't imagine a better motivation," he said. Harper addresses role for coming season After offseason chatter about his role, San Antonio Spurs guard Dylan Harper said he'd follow the coaches' lead this season. "Everyone has a competitive edge to them. But the biggest thing for me is whatever I can do, just like last year, to help the team win," he said. "Whatever position the coaches think is best for me to be in, that's the position I'll happily go in." First look at LeBron in a 76ers uniform New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James is taking questions from reporters on Monday. Here's what he had to say when asked about his initial impressions of his team: "Everybody is on the same page," James said. "We are all speaking the same language." LeBron addressed his role too, saying he's open to whatever the team needs from him to win. "Whatever they need me to do," he said. "The luxury of my game is I can do everything. ... Literally, I can do everything" Kawhi: I was a distraction, ready to move forward In his first public appearance with the Toronto Raptors after a controversy-filled summer, Kawhi Leonard addressed the NBA's investigation into him and his business dealings. "I know why some of you guys came. You want to hear about the investigation. Haliburton: I am 100% healthy Indiana Pacers guard Tyrese Haliburton said Monday that he is healthy and ready for the season. "I am healthy. I am 100%," he said. "There will be no restrictions. That is not news. There is no source. I am the source. I am ready to go for the year." Porzingis out indefinitely in blow to Warriors Golden State Warriors big man Kristaps Porzingis is out indefinitely to open training camp with a health issue, according to the team. In late July, Porzingis agreed to a two-year, $40 million contract with a player option on the second season to return to the Warriors. Brown: KAT, Hart extension talks won't be a distraction After reports surfaced last week that negotiations between the New York Knicks and center Karl-Anthony Towns had hit a stalemate, coach Mike Brown said Monday neither Towns' situation nor Hart's would linger in the locker room. "We talk about everything [with the team]," Brown said. "We don't want to have any elephants in the room." "I'm not involved in it. They'll figure it out. Control what you can control." And here's what Towns said about a potential extension: "I've made it known I want to play here. Been a fan since I was a kid. I'd like to get it done." Hornets GM: Brandon Miller to be ready for training camp After undergoing offseason surgery on his left shoulder, Hornets wing Brandon Miller should be a full participant in training camp and "ready to roll" for opening night, Hornets general manager Jeff Peterson said Monday. Miller, 23, is entering his fourth NBA season after being the No. 2 pick in the 2023 draft. Duren won't be at Pistons media day, start of camp Detroit Pistons All-Star center Jalen Duren is not attending the team's media day on Monday or the start of training camp as his contract standoff continues, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Monday. Duren, a restricted free agent, is declining the team's five-year, $200 million fully guaranteed offer as both sides remain at a stalemate ahead of the Thursday deadline on a one-year, $9.6 million qualifying offer, sources said. James: Maxey, Embiid were factors in joining 76ers LeBron James said his longstanding friendship with All-Star Tyrese Maxey and a desire to help Joel Embiid win his first NBA title played significant roles in his decision to sign a two-year, $8 million contract with the Philadelphia 76ers in July. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into the process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."
