stories.title: JJ Redick sends strong warning to Lakers bench after pathetic 60-second span
stories.summary: Lakers coach JJ Redick made it clear that what happened on Sunday night won’t occur again.
stories.detailText: Lakers head coach JJ Redick made it clear that what happened on Sunday night won’t occur again. And that there are consequences, especially for end-of-bench players, for not being ready to play in an NBA game when their number is called. Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick wasn’t pleased with how his team closed out Sunday’s win over the Raptors. NBAE via Getty Images The Lakers coach thought his team’s lead was safe when he subbed out most of his main rotation players – Austin Reaves, Walker Kessler and Matisse Thybulle – with the Lakers leading by 14 points (123-109) with 1:43 left of their home game against the Raptors. Luka Dončić, who had already scored 41 points by that point, had been out of the game for 45 seconds, with the Lakers and Redick believing the end-of-bench players would put the finishing touches on securing the victory. Los Angeles Lakers head coach JJ Redick had plenty to be frustrated about with how the team’s end-of-bench players performed late in the win over the Raptors. AP Photo/Scott Strazzante Even though the Lakers did eventually beat the Raptors , it didn’t come to fruition as Redick and the team hoped, with the end-of-bench players nearly blowing a double-digit lead in less than a minute. “I won’t make that mistake again,” Redick said. “I’ll leave the guys in. You gotta play to the final buzzer, and if guys are not ready to play, then I just won’t put them in.” After one of the lone rotation players, Quentin Grimes, split a pair of free throws to put the Lakers up 124-109 with 1:24 left, Jamison Battle hit a catch-and-shoot 3-pointer to cut the Raptors’ deficit to 12. JJ Redick on the Lakers' lead being cut from 15 points to 5 in 40 seconds after LAL subbed its main rotation players out against the Raptors, leading to JJ subbing them back in to close the game: "We just didn't do a good job of taking care of the ball in that situation. So I… pic.twitter.com/pUhIHhvMLp — Khobi Price (@khobi_price) November 2, 2026 A failed lob attempt from Grimes to Jarred Vanderbilt that resulted in a turnover turned into another Battle catch-and-shoot 3 in transition that quickly cut the Lakers’ lead to nine points. And a failed inbounds pass by Bronny James led to the Lakers’ lead dropping down to seven after Battle hit a floater on the Raptors’ ensuing possession, making it eight straight points in less than 20 seconds of game time for the 2024 undrafted forward out of Ohio State. Jamison Battle scored eight straight points in less than 20 seconds of game time to make a significant dent in the Lakers’ lead. NBAE via Getty Images Redick had seen enough by the time Jaden Bradley converted an and-1 layup to trim the Raptors’ deficit to six points with 44 seconds left (and five points after making the free throw) after the Lakers led by 15 points just 40 seconds prior. Dončić, Reaves, Kessler and Thybulle all subbed back in for James, Vanderbilt, Jaden Hardy and Cameron Carr ( who was making his NBA debut ) before Bradley shot his free throw. The Lakers did just enough to secure the win with its main players back in the game, but it wasn’t pretty. “A lot of times as a player when you kind of get something like that in that point, you kind of look at it as garbage minutes but the reality is, every time you step on the court, you got to treat it like it’s minutes to play the game,” Kessler said. “Because my rookie and sophomore year, I got put in the garbage minutes and you got to play to the whistle because the reality is you’re only going to get your shot. And I’m not saying that those guys aren’t competitors ‘cause a lot of them are, but they got to be a lot more more fundamental, for sure.”

stories.title: Lakers’ Austin Reaves forced to take headband away from fan for most understandable reason
stories.summary: Luckily, the Lakers fan was a good sport about it.
stories.detailText: The Lakers improved to 5-2 on the young season with a 131-125 win over the Raptors on Sunday night. The score is not indicative of how much Los Angeles controlled the game, which set in motion the most hysterical moment of the game. When Austin Reaves subbed out with 1:43 remaining in the Lakers’ eventual win over the Raptors , he did so with clear intentions of not returning to the game. The biggest tell: The Lakers star guard gave his signature headband to a fan sitting behind the team’s bench, with Reaves expecting to watch the remainder of the game from the sidelines. Austin Reaves (15) had to get his signature headband back when Lakers coach JJ Redick needed to put him back in the game. NBAE via Getty Images That didn’t come to fruition as planned. With their end-of-bench players in the game, the Lakers’ lead was cut from 15 points with 1:24 left to single digits within 20 seconds of game time. Austin Reaves didn’t expect to be needed for the closing stretch. NBAE via Getty Images Coach JJ Redick had seen enough from the reserves when Jaden Bradley converted the and-1 layup that trimmed the Raptors’ deficit to six points with 44 seconds left (and five points after making the free throw), deciding to sub his main rotation players back in to close the game out. Which meant that Reaves had to retrieve his headband as he, Matisse Thybulle, Walker Kessler and Luka Dončić all subbed back in the game with 44 seconds left to secure the victory. Luckily for Reaves, it didn’t appear the fan had any issues with handing the headband back over. The Lakers got the job done after getting their main rotation players back in the game. NBAE via Getty Images With Redick saying he won’t make this mistake again, subbing in players if they aren’t ready to play late in games, it appears to be unlikely that the 6-foot-5 guard will be in this position again. But in case it does, Reaves better hold onto his headband until the game’s officially over.

Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photo by Barry Gossage/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images You wouldn’t think the sky would be falling in most fanbases four games into the season where the team has picked up a win, but here we are with the Phoenix Suns and their 1-3 start. The frustration from the fanbase has gotten so loud that we’ve got the team’s TV play-by-play broadcaster Kevin Ray comparing how to manage the freezing nature of a cold plunge to coping with the early season struggles. With an 0-2 week in the books, reports that there’s growing “frustration” in the locker room over a lack of a true point guard, and with many key players going down with injuries around the NBA, here are some questions we want your answers on: Starting guards trade struggling games In last week’s loss against the Oklahoma City Thunder, Devin Booker had one of the worst games of his career, scoring just three points on seven shots. In the following game, Jalen Green scored just two points on 1/6 shooting from the field, his lowest scoring output as a member of the Suns in a game where he didn’t leave early because of injury. Both games the Suns lost. Coming into the season, the Suns’ lack of point guard in the starting lineup caused some controversy around the team, and with NBA Insider Chris Haynes’ latest report about the backcourt not working well together, many are calling for the team to trade for a point guard or replace Green with Collin Gillespie in the starting lineup, who’s had success playing alongside Devin Booker in the past. If you’re Jordan Ott and the coaching staff, how would you handle the guard controversy? A massive break between games? Phoenix has played the fewest games in the NBA so far, with a lot of that attributed to the 96-hour break they had between their two games this week. The Suns have played just two games since October 25th. In turn, this week will be more intense. They’ll play four games in a six-day span, including their first back-to-back of the year. As a fan, how did you enjoy the massive break between games so early into the season, and how do you think it will impact them as their schedule ramps up? Injuries around the West The Western Conference suffered a bevy of significant injuries in the past week. The Oklahoma City Thunder have lost three starters: Anthony Edwards is expected out for about two months, Jaren Jackson Jr. will be sidelined for the next 5-7 weeks, and Ja Morant is expected to miss nearly all of November. While the Suns remain without Mark Williams, the rest of the roster is healthy, and they’ve known they’d be without Williams more than a month before the season started. How do the injuries impact where you think the Suns stand in the West? Weird, but True The Suns have played four of their last five postseason opponents to start their season. Their only win came against the only team they beat in postseason play, the Golden State Warriors, whom they beat in last year’s 8/9 Play-In game. stories.title: Nets vs. Knicks preview: Nets look to end the streak
stories.summary: The Nets haven’t beaten the Knicks since January 2023. Is tonight the night they end the streak?
stories.detailText: NEW YORK, NEW YORK - JULY 18: Roman Reigns and Jalen Brunson look on in ring during Saturday Night's Main Event at Madison Square Garden on July 18, 2026 in New York, United States. (Photo by Rich Freeda/WWE via Getty Images) | WWE via Getty Images NEW YORK, NEW YORK – JULY 18: Roman Reigns and Jalen Brunson look on in ring during Saturday Night's Main Event at Madison Square Garden on July 18, 2026 in New York, United States. (Photo by Rich Freeda/WWE via Getty Images) | WWE via Getty Images Maybe that one win in Indy will change things for the Brooklyn Nets. Maybe the cross-town rivalry will get the New York Knicks out of their lethargy. But at the moment, the Nets, despite their awful opening, are 1-5, only a game behind the 2-4 world champions. Indeed, if the Nets should upset the Knicks, the two would be tied! Of course. 2026 has been the year of the New York Knicks as everyone’s still riding high from their NBA championship win over the summer. They’ve gotten off to a poor start this season at 2-4 and lost a close one, 98-93 , to LeBron James and the Philadelphia 76ers on Friday night in Philly. Game info and broadcast details Matchup : Brooklyn Nets vs. New York Knicks Date : Monday, November 2, 2026 Time: 7:30 PM EST (6:30 PM CST) Location : Madison Square Garden (New York, NY) TV/Streaming/Radio : YES Network, MSG Network, DAZN, ESPN Radio, WFAN Nets vs. Knicks: Who’s out? Brooklyn Nets Egor Dëmin: OUT — Right leg bone bruise Joshua Jefferson: OUT – G League Assignment Ben Saraf: OUT – G League Assignment Tyler Bilodeau: OUT – G League (Two-Way) Grant Nelson: OUT – G League (Two-Way) New York Knicks Jose Alvarado: Questionable — (left ankle sprain) The Game This isn’t Julius Randle’s first game back at MSG after the big trade a few years ago. But it is his first game back after they won the championship. Should make for an interesting evening for him. Perhaps that will help the Nets in their years long quest to finally beat the Knicks. Brooklyn has not won a game against their crosstown rivals since January 2023 when Randle was a Knick and Kyrie Irving was a Net. Time flies, doesn’t it? For Randle, he’ll look to find his shot. Randle hasn’t shot above 50% from the field since the game against the Cleveland Cavaliers in the second game of the season. Brooklyn needs a lot from Randle when it comes to the quality of shots he can generate and when it comes to holding on to the ball. Randle is sixth in the NBA in turnovers per game at 4.2 a night, and for a Nets offense that has had its struggles, you can’t live with that. Day’ron Sharpe and Mo Wagner will look to put a good outing together against one of the best bigs in basketball. Sharpe collected his first double-double of the season last night in Indiana and for the first time this year, it felt like he was a real presence on the boards. That will be critical going up against Karl-Anthony Towns. KAT has been tremendous as a Knick and is a center that expands the floor and forces opposing bigs into touch choices. Towns hasn’t reached the best version of his game yet this season, but the signs are there and with a few tweaks , the Knicks offense is due to take-off sooner rather than later. The forward matchup ought to be fun. OG Anunoby made himself a household name during the playoffs, but he’s been great for a long time. OG does a bit of everything and will get his fair share of matchups against elite wings. He’ll draw Michael Porter Jr tonight, and MPJ will look to keep Anunoby off-balance. If the game is close late, Porter Jr’s ability to get his own shot will keep the Nets in it and give them a chance to pull off the upset. It’s been a long time since the Nets beat the Knicks, and today would be as good of a time as any to make a change. Player to Watch: Jalen Brunson Life is good when you’re the King of New York. Jalen Brunson was already a beloved figure, but the championship has taken him into the rarified air that few players ever reach. Saturday Night’s Main Event was built primarily on his presence (with a special surprise shout out to KAT and Danhausen!). He’s got a guest appearance on Law and Order: SVU this week. And his NBA Finals run featured some of the greatest guard play you’ll ever see. Brunson’s shooting numbers haven’t joined the party yet this season. His shooting splits are down across the board in his first six games, but give it about a month and a half and he should be back to where his career numbers are. He’s drawing a lot more contact and is getting to the free throw line at the highest rate of his career. Drawing fouls is an art and being a good free throw shooter that can get your own shot and get to the line is worth its weight in gold. Mikel Brown Jr is back and we’ll see how many minutes he plays tonight. Who knows how long the Nets will be managing his minutes, but hopefully they let him loose in his pro debut at the Garden. We’ll see if he gets minutes next to Nolan Traore tonight. Nolan was a bright spot against the Pacers last night and knocked down four three-pointers. His development will go a long way in determining what a future may look like for the Nets, and the more good minutes he puts on the board, the more optimistic Nets fans should feel about his game going forward. stories.title: NBA Power Rankings: Early title favorites, rising contenders and relegation zone candidates
stories.summary: Here's how all 30 teams rank nearly two weeks into the NBA season.
stories.detailText: Nearly two weeks into the NBA season, who has the best shot to win it all? I'll answer that question at the start of every month this season with my NBA Power Rankings here on Yahoo Sports. I've ranked all 30 teams in the order I'd pick them to win the title while also accounting for recent performance. That means the undefeated Grizzlies don't rank first, but it does mean they've taken a big jump from where they were in the preseason. Let's get to it starting with the league's worst teams: East: Atlanta Hawks • Boston Celtics • Brooklyn Nets • Charlotte Hornets • Chicago Bulls • Cleveland Cavaliers • Detroit Pistons • Indiana Pacers • Miami Heat • Milwaukee Bucks • New York Knicks • Orlando Magic • Philadelphia 76ers • Toronto Raptors • Washington Wizards West: Dallas Mavericks • Denver Nuggets • Golden State Warriors • Houston Rockets • LA Clippers • Los Angeles Lakers • Memphis Grizzlies • Minnesota Timberwolves • New Orleans Pelicans • Oklahoma City Thunder • Phoenix Suns • Portland Trail Blazers • Sacramento Kings • San Antonio Spurs • Utah Jazz RELEGATION ZONE CANDIDATES 30. Sacramento Kings Record: 0-6 | Previous rank: 30 The Kings are winless. They didn't even win a preseason game. They've gotten pounded every single night and have very little hope of winning more than one or two of their next 13 games, which means breaking the NBA's worst losing streak to begin a season (0-18) is certainly on the table for Sacramento. For Kings fans to stay sane this year, they can't be worried about the score at the final buzzer. It has to be about the development of rookie point guard Darius Acuff. Straight out of the gates, Acuff is averaging 26.3 points per game, but he's doing it on 24 shots per game. Over the course of the year, Kings fans should obviously root for more epic scoring performances from their rookie guard, but they also need to see him improve his scoring efficiency, develop as a playmaker, and show some heart as a defender. Acuff needs to prove he can be somebody who can impact winning. Or else he's going to earn a reputation: Empty stats scorer. 29. Milwaukee Bucks Record: 1-5 | Previous rank: 29 New Bucks head coach Taylor Jenkins needs to pull the plug on the veterans. Myles Turner looks like he's coasting until he's traded. Tyler Herro ball watches all game long on defense. Kyle Kuzma seems more interested in podcasting and posting online. Why is Jenkins so invested in them? Every other player on this roster is under 30 years old, and has lots to build toward. Kel'el Ware should be fully empowered ahead of Turner, and rookies Brayden Burries and Nate Ament have both shown more than enough flashes to warrant more minutes. Let's see what these kids have. (Hassan Ahmad/Yahoo Sports Illustration) 28. Los Angeles Clippers Record: 1-5 | Previous rank: 28 What matters most to the Clippers this season is the development of rookie point guard Keaton Wagler, and so far you've got to love the way he's just hurtling himself into the paint. All that experience will pay off for him. But everybody else around the league is watching for Brook Lopez, Derrick Jones, Rui Hachimura, and Kris Dunn. The Clippers have individually talented players who could help contenders around the NBA, so there is a chance they will be able to restore some of the draft picks lost from the Aspiration punishment. 27. Chicago Bulls Record: 1-5 | Previous rank: 25 "I'm 20 and I've never been a loser in my whole life so I'm going to try my best to make sure that doesn't happen, and I'm not ever going to accept being a loser," Bulls rookie Caleb Wilson said on Friday. "This is my job to be a leader on this team and it's all going to start with me, I know that. It's partially my fault that we started off the way we did, whether I'm the youngest on the team or not. I take ownership for that and it won't happen again." If you're a Bulls fan, you have got to love those words from Wilson. He plays with contagious energy and enthusiasm, and he's shown major star flashes ever since he was drafted. But I'm worried the trio of Wilson, Matas Buzelis, and Josh Giddey is simply fundamentally flawed. None of them are pure point guards. None of them are knockdown shooters. And with Wilson being empowered as the guy, both Buzelis and Giddey have struggled to continue progressing in the ways they showed last season. Maybe they figure it out. But so far, it's leading to more losses than expected. 26. Brooklyn Nets Record: 1-5 | Previous rank: 26 You have to find silver linings when you're watching a bad basketball team, and I hope Nets fans are enjoying the Nolan Traoré experience. It feels like you're watching a game at 1.5x speed when he has the ball, which allows him to create advantages for his team that a lot of guards can't. The most encouraging thing about Sunday's 16-point outing was the fact he was hitting his spot-up 3-pointers. Shooting was the concern for Traoré entering the NBA, but now he's at 39% on this young season after going 4-for-8 in Brooklyn's first win. His mechanics look pure — he was even no-dipping on his 3s. If he keeps it up, the Nets very well might have their point guard of the future. 25. New Orleans Pelicans Record: 2-4 | Previous rank: 27 We're working with the tiniest of sample sizes at this early point of the season. But the Pelicans have a +19.2 net rating in minutes with Herb Jones on the floor and a -14.5 net rating without him. He played under 20 minutes in their first three games, and the Pelicans went 0-3. He played over 25 in each of the last two, and the Pelicans won both. If the Pelicans still can't score at an elite level — in large part due to a lack of shooting across this roster — then they should lean into playing the best defense they can. And that means Jamahl Mosley needs to put Herb on the floor as much as possible. IT LOOKED BETTER ON PAPER 24. Utah Jazz Record: 1-5 | Previous rank: 21 A few weeks before the season, Krysyan Edler was nice enough to interview me about the Jazz for The Deseret News. She quoted me saying: "I just don't see how this team is bad again. I just think they have too many good players, both young and proven." I wish those words were totally fabricated, but I totally said that. I bought the hype that the Jazz would be a great story this season. And so far, it's looking like I was dead wrong. Jaren Jackson Jr. is already sidelined with a torn MCL. Jusuf Nurkić hasn't played a game yet. Lauri Markkanen looks like a shell of his former self. And all the young guys haven't been anything special. Darryn Peterson has been the worst of the top four picks. Ace Bailey and Keyonte George look like they've plateaued. Maybe Will Hardy actually isn't any good as a coach? Once again, the Jazz appear to be headed for the NBA Draft Lottery. 23. Phoenix Suns Record: 1-3 | Previous rank: 20 NBA reporter Chris Haynes recently said "there's some growing frustration" in the Suns' locker room because the roster "does not have a point guard that can organize that offense." Umm. Have the players in that locker room forgotten about Collin Gillespie? Look, Gillespie is no Chris Paul. But he started 58 games last year, posted a 2.9 assist-to-turnover ratio, and vibed well with Devin Booker. This season, Gillespie has been moved to the bench in favor of Jalen Green, who is a black hole offensively. It makes zero sense. The Suns are posting a 110.2 offensive rating in the 92 minutes that Booker and Green have shared the floor. That number is 128.3 in the 43 minutes Booker has shared the floor with Gillespie without Green. Maybe, just maybe, the Suns should do a lot more of that. 22. Orlando Magic Record: 2-4 | Previous rank: 19 How soon is too soon to worry about Franz Wagner's jumper? Wagner has made only six of his 31 triples this season (19.4%) and mechanically his shot looks completely broken with 67 moving parts happening all at once from the moment he catches the ball. Wagner is in the sixth season of his career and still hasn't been able to translate his soft touch from the line (85%) and floater range (nearly 50%) to the perimeter. He's at 32.1% for his career. But it's never been as bad as now. Paolo Banchero's absence is also really felt since he can catch fire from the perimeter, covering for Wagner's primary weakness. The Magic are badly missing him, and until he returns it's hard to feel much confidence in this team. But Banchero is streaky himself, and his averages really aren't any better since he also goes through severe cold stretches. We might just be finding out that Wagner and Banchero aren't compatible. ASK ME AFTER THANKSGIVING 21. Indiana Pacers Record: 2-5 | Previous rank: 14 Tyrese Haliburton returned to the floor and immediately looked like Tyrese Haliburton. But he's already sidelined by a hamstring issue, and now the Pacers already look like the same 19-win Haliburtonless team from last year. Indiana is being outscored by 8.7 points per 100 possessions in the minutes without Haliburton this season. For as long as he's gone, it's not looking like it'll get any better. 20. Atlanta Hawks Record: 3-4 | Previous rank: 15 The bullish case for Atlanta this year was largely dependent on Jalen Johnson taking another step forward as a player. He averaged 22.5 points, 10.3 rebounds, and 7.9 assists last year, earning himself a spot on an All-NBA team. It's been a step back this year. He's not scoring with as much efficiency, his volume is down, and the rest of the roster isn't making up for it. The Hawks aren't shooting 3s well. Nickeil Alexander-Walker remains more of an off-ball talent. And CJ McCollum is playing like he's 35 years old. If Johnson doesn't take another step forward, it's unlikely anyone else on this team will. 19. Charlotte Hornets Record: 3-4 | Previous rank: 16 I'm having a hard time judging the Hornets, given the fact that both Kon Knueppel and Coby White have yet to play this season (White will make his debut on Monday). It doesn't seem fair to make any assumptions about what this roster is supposed to perform like without two of its three best players. But it's undeniably encouraging that the Hornets have managed to pull off three wins and competed against both the Pistons and Sixers despite having a depleted roster. Once this team is whole, hopefully Brandon Miller's scoring efficiency can improve, and the rotation will fall into its intended place. FUN AND FIESTY 18. Washington Wizards Record: 3-3 | Previous rank: 23 So much for all the talk about AJ Dybantsa not being an impactful defensive player. In his second game with the Wizards, he had seven rebounds and five deflections. Both Brandon Miller and Naz Reid had a hard time creating quality shots against him. Dybantsa moved rapidly against Miller on the perimeter, and battled hard with Reid on multiple post-ups. We know Dybantsa can score and pass. But the fact he's already bringing it defensively is answering the biggest question about him. 17. Portland Trail Blazers Record: 4-1 | Previous rank: 18 Conversations about Portland this preseason were usually about Tom Dundon's ownership drama, the comebacks of Ja Morant and Damian Lillard, and what to expect from a new head coach in Micah Nori. But perhaps the best story on the team so far has been Deni Avdija, who continues getting better after his breakout last season. Deni is still driving to the basket with a relentless force, but he's also now shooting 3s better. When I interviewed Deni to finish last season, I asked him about the struggles he experienced as a shooter last year — he made 31.8% of his 3s. "You're hurting me by saying those numbers," Avdija said sarcastically before continuing. "I know it's going to come back. I am going to keep putting in the work." He clearly has. So far this year, he's up to 37.5% on all 3s and over 40% on catch-and-shoot 3s. Given the fact that he's going to be sharing the court with other guards all year long, it's especially important that he can space the floor to take another leap as an All-Star. 16. Golden State Warriors Record: 4-3 | Previous rank: 22 Isn't it such a blessing that Steph Curry still looks like Steph Curry on the basketball court? He's averaging 29 points per game on 69.1% true shooting, and the Warriors are still fun. But it's not at all Steph. It's rookie Yaxel Lendeborg, who is helping turn what was supposed to be a grim year in Golden State into a beautiful one. Lendeborg brings a versatile skill set to the floor with an inside-outside scoring game and a selfless passing gene that must make Steve Kerr have goosebumps. Lendeborg had 37 points on Sunday night and is averaging big numbers with 22.3 points, 7.3 rebounds, and 3.7 assists. Lendeborg has been so good early on this season that it's hard not to wonder if he could even contend for an All-Star spot as a rookie. The last time that happened was in 2011 when Blake Griffin did it with the Clippers. 15. Memphis Grizzlies Record: 6-0 | Previous rank: 24 The Grizzlies remain the only undefeated team in the NBA, but they still are ranked outside the top 10 in these Power Rankings. Why? Largely because of the reason I stated in the introduction: I'm not overreacting to everything that happened in the first two weeks of the season. But also, let's just be honest: They have two wins against Utah, two wins against Sacramento, and wins against Portland and Golden State. Their next two opponents are New Orleans and Indiana. They might be 8-0 going into a three-game stretch against Oklahoma City, Toronto, and Denver. Those matchups will be better barometer tests for the young Grizzlies team. But there's no denying how much reason for optimism there is. Ty Jerome has built on his strong end to last season . Cedric Coward has refound his 3-pointer, and Cam Boozer looks like he's going to be a multi-time All-Star for a decade-plus in the NBA. I predicted Memphis would hit the over this season. So in some regards, I'm not too surprised that they're looking good. But undefeated? With the best record in the league? We'll see if that can be sustained. 14. Dallas Mavericks Record: 4-2 | Previous rank: 17 Is Cooper Flagg already a top-10 player at just 19 years old? This season we've watched Flagg lead Dallas to wins while outplaying Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Giannis Antetokounmpo, and he handed Houston its first loss behind a 33-point, 9-rebound, 6-assist effort. What we're seeing from Flagg right now follows a natural trajectory. He got way better after turning 18 years old at Duke. Then over the final 26 games of his rookie season, he averaged 25 points, 7 rebounds, and 5 assists. And so far this year, he's averaging 26.8 points, 6 rebounds, and 6.6 assists on elite scoring efficiency, an even better assist-to-turnover ratio, and more impactful defense. What's this production gonna look like by the end of the season when so far he's clearly been one of the league's 5-to-10 best players? People will say I am being reactionary, but Flagg has been on this path for multiple years now. So no matter where he actually ranks today: Flagg has arrived. FALLING CONTENDERS 13. Toronto Raptors Record: 3-3 | Previous rank: 10 The mysteriousness around Kawhi Leonard's health is the whole reason why it's very tough to pick this team to represent the East in the NBA Finals. Leonard might return midway through the year and look like a top player, just like he did last year with the Clippers. But who's to say he's going to make it to the finish line? Kawhi so rarely ever does. So as much promise as there is in Toronto because of their youth and Scottie Barnes continuing to ascend, the Raptors are 3-3. And they're without their best player with no guarantees they'll ever have him when they need him most. 12. Cleveland Cavaliers Record: 4-2 | Previous rank: 11 It's pretty crazy that Mario Hezonja looks like a better free-agent signing than Peyton Watson. But it's true. Through six games, Hezonja is playing hard, providing secondary scoring, and not turning the ball over. Meanwhile, Watson has made only 17% of his 3s, has offered very little in the shot creation department, and hasn't lived up to his billing as a defensive player. In a Cavs loss against the Sixers, Watson was unable to stay in front of Jaylen Brown down the stretch. The Cavs have been solid to start the year, but they really need Watson to turn things around soon. He was their big-money, free-agent signing. Hezonja was a no-risk, minimum signing. But he's doing what he was signed to do, and he still can't do the things they need from Watson. 11. Miami Heat Record: 2-4 | Previous rank: 7 The Heat are still in the process of figuring out who they are. They started out 0-4, and they've won two in a row against Atlanta and Indiana. Head coach Erik Spoelstra already began to tweak the system against Atlanta. They ran 57 pick-and-rolls. Prior to that, their average per game was 23.5. Against Atlanta, Giannis had 24 screens, more than he did in the other four games combined. In Miami's next win against Indiana, the team set 37 on-ball screens. So the Heat are clearly experimenting between their innovative screenless system that we saw last year by integrating some more traditional pick-and-roll concepts. The Heat kick off a five-game West Coast road trip starting Monday night in Los Angeles before returning home for a tough homestand against four contending teams. The next few weeks will tell us a lot about who this Heat team really is. And if it continues struggling, you can expect a free fall in the next edition of these Power Rankings. 10. Denver Nuggets Record: 3-2 | Previous rank: 8 After Nikola Jokić hyperextended his knee last season, his 3-pointer never came back once he returned to the court. Jokić shot 44% from 3 prior to the injury, comparable to his 42% clip the year prior. But after he returned, that number plummeted to 32% during the season, then 19% during the playoffs. Right now this season? Twenty-one percent. I wrote about the domino effect of Jokić's lost shot during the playoffs, and how that was hurting Jokić's formerly potent two-man action with Jamal Murray. The Minnesota defense was able to sag off Jokić, dare him to shoot, and take away driving lanes for Murray and everyone else. The same thing is happening this year. When Jokić screens for Murray, the Nuggets are scoring 1.02 points per play. That's their lowest number since the 2019-20 season, back when people still questioned whether Jokić could even lead a championship team. If his jumper doesn't return, he may never again. 9. Los Angeles Lakers Record: 5-2 | Previous rank: 6 Look at Austin Reaves' stat line on paper, and you'll like what you see. He's averaging 23.1 points on 66.9% true shooting. But the Lakers are posting a dismal offensive rating of just 100 in the minutes Reaves is on the floor without Luka Dončić. That's down from 137.7 with both Reaves and Dončić and 112 with just Dončić. The big question coming into this season was about whether the Lakers could survive defensively. They can't also have issues with their offense when their best player isn't on the floor. It needs to be resolved, or they may prove to not even be a fringe contender. RISING CONTENDERS 8. Houston Rockets Record: 6-1 | Previous rank: 12 Houston is leading the NBA in offensive rating despite shooting the fifth-fewest amount of 3s. Oh, how times have changed from the days of James Harden when the Rockets were leading the league in 3s by an enormous margin. Now, the Rockets just favor quality. As a result, they are fourth in the NBA in 3-point percentage. The Rockets won 52 games last year without Fred VanVleet and with Steven Adams missing the majority of the year. Adams still hasn't played this year, so head coach Ime Udoka hasn't been able to turn to his two-big lineup that inhales rebounds with Adams and Alperen Şengün. Once that layer is added to the Rockets, this team could look even more dynamic than it already does as one of the best teams in basketball early on this season. 7. Detroit Pistons Record: 5-1 | Previous rank: 13 If Victor Wembanyama doesn't reach the 65-game threshold, Ausar Thompson very well might be the Defensive Player of the Year. The Pistons have the best defensive rating in the NBA and they're 10.6 points better with Ausar on the floor — 97.8 with and 108.4 without. But as much love as Thompson's defense routinely gets, I'm also intrigued by his offense. He still can't shoot. But the Pistons added enough other shooters on the team that they're now putting Thompson into a Draymond-like role in the post area, empowering him to spray the ball all around the floor. Ausar is averaging a career-high 5.2 assists this season. They're getting the most out of him, and they're at their best when he's in with his strange but awesome game. 6. Boston Celtics Record: 5-1 | Previous rank: 9 It sounds ridiculous to say, but Jayson Tatum and Paul George look like they have more synergy on the court together than Tatum and Jaylen Brown ever did. Of course, Tatum and Brown won a championship together. Of course, durability is the whole concern about George. We'll see how long he can stay on the court. But Boston's vision for the Tatum-George pairing has been blatantly obvious so far this season. George simply accepts his secondary role and offers more complementary skills as a knockdown 3-point shooter and a superior defensive player. George is making 38.8% of his 3s this season, and he's second in the NBA with 5.5 deflections per game. Meanwhile, Tatum is posting All-NBA numbers once again with 28.3 points, 7.7 assists, and 6 boards. I LIKED THEM BETTER TWO WEEKS AGO 5. Minnesota Timberwolves Record: 4-3 | Previous rank: 5 I was extremely high on the Timberwolves entering this season, and I was having the most fun watching them of any team in basketball before Anthony Edwards was sidelined for at least two months thanks to knee surgery. It's scary now, especially because Rudy Gobert also looks like a shell of his former self as he deals with back spasms. The Timberwolves' defense has been horrific in non-Gobert minutes for years, so they have to deal with his issue while also navigating the offense without Ant. All the talk ahead of this season was about how deep the league was this year, and how health would be the determining factor in seeding in each conference. Well, the Timberwolves went from a team in the conversation to compete for the top seed to one that will need to battle to stay out of the play-in before Ant can return. Gulp! 4. New York Knicks Record: 2-4 | Previous rank: 3 Are you worried, Knicks fans? I'm not. It's a slow start to the year for Jalen Brunson. OG Anunoby and Mikal Bridges aren't hitting 3s yet. Mike Brown is still figuring out the best lineup combinations with this tweaked bench unit. It's a funky start for the defending champions, but they've played some really competitive games against some really tough teams in the East. Moving them down just one spot seems appropriate. If these struggles continue into December, then there might be something to seriously worry about. 3. Oklahoma City Thunder Record: 4-2 | Previous rank: 1 One morning you can wake up as a fan and feel like your team is about to go on an epic revenge tour across the NBA all year long. The next day, it'll feel like you're experiencing a lost season without any guarantee of ever making it back to the championship. That's where Thunder fans are after losing Jalen Williams for likely the entire season and Chet Holmgren for a large chunk of the season. Oklahoma City is still built to win a lot of games this year. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander is about to go ham. But the Thunder's hopes of winning a title again certainly took a big ding, given their injuries — Cason Wallace is also sidelined. The absences also cast doubt over their future. Williams has effectively missed two straight seasons. It's very hard to get back to the level that you were at prior to missing so much time on the court. Holmgren has now played in only 56% of all possible games in his NBA career. Gilgeous-Alexander is about as durable, reliable, and consistent as any superstar. But his co-stars are the opposite. THE FAVORITES 2. Philadelphia 76ers Record: 6-1 | Previous rank: 4 After deciding to join the Sixers, LeBron James made it clear that Tyrese Maxey was the biggest draw. Maxey is certainly living up to the hype by averaging 29.6 points on 60.4% true shooting. He's an early Clutch Player of the Year candidate thanks to his late-game buckets across multiple wins, and Sixers fans are already hyping him up as an MVP candidate. Regardless of how this year progresses, it's been rather amazing to see his growth. He entered the NBA with such blazing speed but he knows how to better control it now, and his growing skill level as a scorer allows him to get buckets from any spot on the floor. The Sixers needed Maxey to keep ascending to be true contenders, and he certainly looks like he has. 1. San Antonio Spurs Record: 4-2 | Previous rank: 2 Mitch Johnson's decision to start all three guards — De'Aaron Fox, Stephon Castle, and Dylan Harper — came as somewhat of a surprise around the NBA. So far it's working. The Spurs have a 122.5 offensive rating and 96.6 defensive rating with those three on the floor in 66 minutes alongside Victor Wembanyama. The three guards have, curiously, yet to play a single minute all together without Wemby, though. Instead, it's been one or two together, just like last year. But unlike last year, they've struggled. In every single lineup combination without Wembanyama on the floor, the Spurs have just a 105.9 offensive rating and a 123.5 defensive rating. It's no surprise their defense gets significantly worse. This happened last year too. But the offense didn't crater quite like this — it did by only 5.8. We're working with small samples, but the non-Wemby minutes are worth watching on the offensive end. Nonetheless, this concern is a nitpick compared to the problems facing other contenders and the Spurs rightfully move to the top of the Power Rankings.

teamStories.title: Debunk or double down? Judging 10 early-season NBA overreactions
teamStories.summary: A 29-year-old is the NBA's next breakout star. Miami's Giannis era is already cooked. And so are the Thunder, Knicks and Warriors. Which overreactions are valid?
teamStories.detailText: Welcome to the final days of October, featuring falling leaves, early sunsets, Halloween decorations illuminating the night -- and the yearly pastime of overreacting to the first week of a new NBA season . After all, small sample size theatre has provided early gems such as: The sky is falling in Oklahoma City , New York and Miami ! The three-guard experiment in San Antonio needs to go! Charlotte is already better without LaMelo Ball ! Ty Jerome ? Ty Jerome! With those early storylines and more in mind, let's examine 10 popular overreactions to the young 2026-27 season -- and determine which have staying power. ( Note: stats through Tuesday's games .) The Miami Heat will finish with their worst record since 2008. Zach Kram: Not an overreaction For reference, 2007-08 was the last time the Heat finished with fewer than 37 wins, the season that they tanked down the stretch to go 15-67 in a futile attempt to land Derrick Rose in the draft. Merely by the law of averages, the 2026-27 Heat are bound to improve. They've had the seventh-worst shooting luck on offense, according to GeniusIQ tracking, and the second-worst shooting luck on defense. Miami is actually forcing teams into tough shots, but its opponents have been on fire regardless, making 53% of their midrange shots and 40% of their 3s, per Cleaning the Glass. On the other hand, the Heat's offense has been stuck in the mud even accounting for that poor shooting luck, and guard Davion Mitchell is the only role player who looks comfortable playing with Giannis Antetokounmpo . There's time for that to change -- but as of Wednesday, ESPN's Basketball Power Index predicts the Heat will finish the season with just 38 wins. That's already down from 46 projected wins in the preseason, and just one ahead of this historical franchise benchmark. Ben Golliver: Overreaction Let's be clear: The Antetokounmpo era in South Beach is off to an atrocious start. Instead of building off its blockbuster trade for the two-time MVP with a transformative offseason, the Heat lost Norman Powell to the Chicago Bulls in free agency and settled for adding Klay Thompson , who is a shell of his former self at age 36. On the court, it's already clear that the Heat need another proven ball handler and more shooting, and Antetokounmpo needs more time to jell with Bam Adebayo . Despite all those challenges, it's reasonable to give Heat coach Erik Spoelstra and his staff a long runway . Antetokounmpo's need to dominate the ball has clashed with the free-flowing offensive system that Miami utilized in 2025-26, and several veteran players seem to be easing into the new season. Spoelstra is a tinkerer who has conjured winning records from less talented rosters, and he'll be willing to trust his younger options if Miami's offensive struggles persist. It's probably best to withhold judgment until after the Heat's upcoming trip out West. If the Heat can't get right against teams such as the LA Clippers , Sacramento Kings , Golden State Warriors and Utah Jazz , sound the alarm. There is some good news: Antetokounmpo has been very productive in the early going, averaging 27.6 points, 11.2 rebounds and 4.6 assists after missing most of last season due to injuries. The Oklahoma City Thunder 's title hopes are gone without Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace . Kram: Not an overreaction Earlier this week, I went into more depth about the impact of these two long-term injuries on Oklahoma City's title chances. The simplified version: The Thunder's winning formula over the past few seasons has been to combine MVP-level offense from Gilgeous-Alexander with the best defense in the league. The collective loss of Williams, Wallace and Luguentz Dort (via summer trade) bends that second factor out of shape. Yes, centers Chet Holmgren and Isaiah Hartenstein still form an imposing backline, and Alex Caruso (currently out with an ankle sprain ) remains a singular defensive force. But the rest of Oklahoma City's perimeter rotation is now so thin, with enough defensive questions, that I would be surprised if it won another title -- barring a return from one of those injured starters before the playoffs or a significant in-season trade. Golliver: (emotional) overreaction Yes, it sure felt as if the sky was falling Monday when Thunder general manager Sam Presti announced that Williams and Wallace are out for the foreseeable future with significant injuries . That's no way to launch a title chase. After those injuries and the offseason trades of Dort, Aaron Wiggins and Isaiah Joe , the Thunder are down five of their top six players by minutes logged during the 2024-25 championship season. Oof. But there's an awful lot of talent remaining around Gilgeous-Alexander, who has been sensational to start this season. Oklahoma City showed its resolve by beating Phoenix on Monday night, and it's worth noting it was only one win from reaching the Finals last year despite an injury-plagued season and postseason for Williams. Presti has picks and tradeable contracts to invest in stop-gap additions before the trade deadline, but he also has a deep roster that was built for the long haul. Count out the Thunder at your own peril. Ty Jerome will be an All-Star. Golliver: Overreaction Only a jerk would root against Jerome, who looks destined for a career year after surviving countless fits and starts to get here. But the Memphis Grizzlies ' schedule has been about as soft as it gets to start the season: The Jazz look poised to give up 30 points to any opposing guard, while the Warriors' injury issues and the Kings' general dysfunction disqualify them from being quality wins. Jerome is a talented scorer who more than earned this promotion to lead ball handler, but let's check back in a few weeks. The good news: LeBron James and Kawhi Leonard left the Western Conference over the summer, so there are more available All-Star spots than usual. Kram: Not an overreaction Jerome wasn't an All-Star last season, of course, because he played only 15 games. But he has been a star-level offensive player for a while now, even if few people recognized it until he started averaging 30 points. Here are the NBA's leaders in offensive box plus-minus for the 2025-26 campaign: Nikola Jokic Shai Gilgeous-Alexander Ty Jerome Luka Doncic Giannis Antetokounmpo Kawhi Leonard Victor Wembanyama Stephen Curry Jamal Murray Donovan Mitchell It doesn't matter when Jimmy Butler III returns -- the Golden State Warriors are cooked. Golliver: Not an overreaction The Warriors finally got their first win of the season Monday, but their opening week has been disheartening. With Butler, Kristaps Porzingis and several players missing time with injuries or ailments, the Warriors sat Curry on a back-to-back and rolled out a starting lineup featuring Yaxel Lendeborg , Brandon Williams , Will Richard , Gui Santos and Graham Ike on Saturday against the Phoenix Suns . That five-man group -- great fodder for Charles Barkley on "Who he play for?" -- will combine to earn less than $20 million this season. Meanwhile, Butler ($56 million) and Porzingis ($19.5 million) are missing in action. There's no way to overcome that math. Kram: Not an overreaction We finally agree, Ben. I'm not especially surprised by the Warriors' predicament because this seemed like a gap year from the start, due to all their injury issues and the lack of any real upgrades over the summer. (Aside from Lendeborg, who looks incredible as a rookie.) Maybe they can stick around the play-in race because the West looks shallower than usual -- the Jazz might also be cooked if Lauri Markkanen and Jaren Jackson Jr . are out for a while -- but Golden State's most important goal should be setting itself up for greater success in 2027-28. The San Antonio Spurs will kill their three-guard starting lineup by Thanksgiving. Kram: Overreaction I tend to think debates about starting lineups are overblown because of how much teams mix and match over the course of a game; lo and behold, the guard trio of De'Aaron Fox , Dylan Harper and Stephon Castle has shared the court for just 43 minutes across four games this season. And while it's way too early to come to significant conclusions using net rating, it's not as if the Spurs have struggled in those minutes. They're plus-15.4 with that three-guard lineup, according to databallr. If San Antonio's coaching staff believes it needs to keep Fox, Harper and Castle in the starting lineup for intangible reasons, then there's no evidence yet that that's a bad idea. Golliver: Overreaction Spurs coach Mitch Johnson could be headed for a real saga that might take months to play out. Of course, the critical decision is whether to start Fox, Harper or both point guards. But Johnson could also buy time for that duo to work things out by swapping Devin Vassell for Tobias Harris or Julian Champagnie . Given Fox's enormous salary and Harper's potential, San Antonio must exhaust every possibility before shifting one guard to the bench. Sacramento Kings coach Doug Christie won't make it to the new year. Golliver: Not an overreaction There are so many red flags coming out of Sacramento that it's starting to look like an Olympics opening ceremony. Naturally, the central tension concerns rookie guard Darius Acuff Jr . and veterans Domantas Sabonis and Zach LaVine . The Kings have turned Acuff loose for 93(!) shots in his first four career games with hopes he will develop into a franchise guard, but his more experienced teammates have good reason to wonder whether that's the best approach to winning. Christie is stuck, and Ben Simmons ' preseason Achilles tear made a tough job even tougher. The Kings look destined to be the NBA's worst team, and that level of ineptitude typically prompts a response from owner Vivek Ranadivé. Kram: Not an overreaction The Kings have let go of five coaches since Ranadivé bought the team in 2013. Two firings came at the end of a season (George Karl in 2016 and Dave Joerger in 2019), but the other three came early in a campaign: Luke Walton (2021) in November and Michael Malone (2014) and Mike Brown (2024) in December. That pattern tells me there's greater than a 50% chance that Christie won't make it to 2027. The New York Knicks won't get out of the first round. Kram: Overreaction I predicted before the season that New York would win fewer regular-season games than a year ago, so I can't profess to be surprised by their sub-.500 start against a tough schedule. The greatest on-court problem for the Knicks is their 25th-ranked offense, but I expect a prompt turnaround: They rank last in making just 30% of their midrange shots, per Cleaning the Glass, after ranking fifth at 45% with largely the same roster a year ago. In looking ahead to the postseason, moreover, I would have to see a much larger sample of struggles to consider the likelihood that New York won't be favored in any playoff matchup in the East. The competition will be tougher this year, but the Knicks are proven playoff performers. Golliver: Not an overreaction This one is more about vibes than hard analytics. As is often the case for defending champions, the Knicks have had a challenging opening week schedule filled with marquee opponents. In that context, the 2-3 start really isn't the end of the world. New York was in competitive games against aspiring contenders in the 76ers and Celtics last week and then handed the Detroit Pistons their first loss on Tuesday. But the Knicks' inability to pull out those close games was a reminder of just how charmed their 2026 postseason was from start to finish. Jalen Brunson seemingly hit every big shot he needed to hit, and the one time Brunson didn't come through, OG Anunoby was right there for the one-in-a-million tip-in. Time after time, the Knicks cheated death with second-half comebacks. That doesn't feel like a sustainable formula now that they've got the target on their backs. Owner James Dolan has also operated like a man who is comfortable with one ring rather than desperate to add another. Trying to win back-to-back championships has exhausted younger teams than the Knicks in recent years, so no one should be all that surprised if they run out of gas or encounter season-altering injuries before May. Offseason trades made the Charlotte Hornets ' current roster better . Kram: Not an overreaction (although I'm prepared for Ball to make this statement look silly) We all thought Charlotte's surprising offseason trades were made with an eye toward the future. After all, the franchise dealt two foundational players and their two highest-salaried players in Ball and Miles Bridges . But the Hornets received so much flexibility and so many valuable draft assets in return that the "one step back, two steps forward" approach made sense. We might have been giving the Hornets' present-day roster short shrift with that assessment. Charlotte has a winning record despite receiving zero minutes from its starting backcourt, as Coby White and Kon Knueppel deal with injuries. Brandon Miller appears to have taken a leap after signing a five-year rookie extension. And offseason additions Naz Reid and Grayson Allen , who came to Charlotte as part of the Ball and Bridges trades, have combined to average 36.3 points while making 44% of their 3-pointers. Reid, in particular, represents a meaningful upgrade over Bridges at power forward. Golliver: Overreaction The jury is still out on the Hornets given the injuries you mentioned and their weak quality of competition to date. With that said, the decision to trade Bridges is already shaping up to be one of those moves they will never regret. Charlotte's short-term success will be determined by Miller's ability to consistently flex his muscles as an alpha scorer and Knueppel's comfort handling greater playmaking duties. Beyond that, Hornets ownership must demonstrate a willingness to spend to build around that budding duo. The Ball trade could wind up as a win-win for Charlotte and Minnesota, but at some point, the Hornets will need to prioritize talent acquisition and retention rather than careful cap management. Otherwise, they're spinning their wheels. Walker Kessler should be on Team USA in 2028. Golliver: Not an overreaction Before the season, the Lakers argued that Kessler was worth paying a premium price in draft picks in their summer sign-and-trade with the Jazz because it's incredibly difficult to find centers at his age (25) with the ability to finish plays on offense and credibly protect the paint on defense. Grant Hill, Spoelstra and USA Basketball would be wise to target big men with that exact skill set for the 2028 Olympics in Los Angeles, especially if Joel Embiid , Anthony Davis and James opt not to return after winning gold in Paris. Adebayo, Holmgren, Jackson and Evan Mobley could all be in the mix, but Kessler brings a level of sheer size and physicality that those players lack. Wouldn't it be helpful to have a traditional center to deploy with Wembanyama and Jokic looming as threats to the U.S. dynasty? Kram: Overreaction You cited the Grizzlies' schedule when cautioning about Jerome's hot start. I'll do the same for Kessler, whose two big games to date came against a Warriors team that didn't start a center and a Clippers team with Isaiah Jackson in the middle. That's not exactly Wembanyama- and Jokic-level competition. Kessler does have international experience, as he was a deep reserve for the unsuccessful 2023 World Cup squad. I believe he's on the long list of American big men for 2028, but I would need much more evidence to place him higher in the pecking order. The Chicago Bulls will be the worst team in the East. Golliver: Not an overreaction For all the preseason talk about improved parity this season thanks to the new lottery rules , there are still some pretty bad teams. The Bulls, Bucks and Nets have all looked like viable contenders to finish with the conference's worst record. (And yet, somehow, the Heat have been harder to watch than all of them.) The scary part about Chicago's start is how thoroughly Toronto and Boston thumped the Bulls. While the Bulls want to play fast under new coach Tiago Splitter, they're just getting completely run off the court by good teams. There's obviously no reason to panic if the blowout losses mount: Caleb Wilson should be encouraged to play free and make mistakes, and Chicago's new front office should focus on which of its veteran players look like long-term fits around the promising rookie forward. And is it too early to predict the Bulls will be getting rid of players at the trade deadline? Kram: Overreaction The Bulls rank dead last in offensive efficiency, but I believe that's more a product of bad luck than bad process. According to GeniusIQ tracking, the Bulls rank fourth in quantified shot probability, which accounts for factors such as location, defender distance and shooter talent. But the Bulls have underperformed that shot quality by 11.1%, which ranks last by a mile. For context, the largest gap for any team over the full 2025-26 season was just 1.7% -- so Chicago's shotmaking is bound to improve. That doesn't mean I think the Bulls will reach the play-in tournament or anything so lofty. But I do believe that they'll play more like a typical rebuilding team going forward, rather than losing every other game by blowout margins.

teamStories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO, TX -OCTOBER 31: Victor Wembanyama #1 of the San Antonio Spurs dunks over Trey Lyles #41 of the Minnesota Timberwolves in the second half at Frost Bank Center on October 31: 2026 in San Antonio, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, User is consenting to terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. (Photo by Ronald Cortes/Getty Images) | Getty Images Welcome to Week in Review: a Monday feature that looks back at the week that was for the San Antonio Spurs , takes a look at the week ahead, and more. Enjoy! Week 1 : It wasn’t the ideal start to the season for the defending Western Conference Finals champions. With Victor Wembanyama not looking like himself (among other issues), they got throttled at home by a fleetingly healthy Thunder squad and lost a heartbreaker in Austin to the Rockets before finally getting their first win of the season against a depleted Mavs team in Dallas. Week #: 4-2 (3-0, 6th in West ) 130-113 win vs. Sacramento Kings There may be no better team to “get right” against than the Kings, and the Spurs made quick work of the annual cellar dwellers (which was a good thing considering it was the first night of a back-to-back). Wemby began his bounce-back by dominating the paint on his way to 29 points, and Julian Champagnie tied his franchise record for three-pointers in a half with 8 in the first. 117-111 OT win at Utah Jazz The Spurs looked lethargic the next night against a shorthanded Jazz team, although they had the excuse of a rest disadvantage and not having time to acclimate to the elevation change. Regardless, after enduring another big game from noted Spurs killer Keyonte George, they woke up and dominated in overtime, with Devin Vassell hitting several key shots down the stretch and Wemby dominating his way to 36 points, including finally hitting some threes. 121-111 win vs. Minnesota Timberwolves Not to be outdone, Geralt if Rivia Wemby took it another step further on Halloween night with 43 points and 6 blocks against a Timberwolves squad that was missing Anthony Edwards and Rudy Gobert (not that the latter has proven to a Wemby stopper). As with all four wins so far, the Spurs left a little something to be desired on the consistency front and weren’t as dominant has they could have been considering the opponents/injuries, but you accept the baby steps (for now). Power Rankings John Schuhmann, NBA.com — N/A (last week: 6) coming soon Law Murray, The Athletic — 4 (last week: 12) The Spurs handled their business in three spots where they should have handled their business: a woeful Kings team, a short-handed Utah team and a short-handed Timberwolves team traveling on zero days’ rest. Still, San Antonio got impressive performances from Victor Wembanyama, culminating in a career-high 34 field goal attempts against the Timberwolves. The Spurs will look much deeper whenever Tobias Harris can get back. Kurt Helin, NBC Sports — 7 (last week: 8) San Antonio has found its footing somewhat after a slow start, and now boasts a top-10 offense and defense. And it has done that without the Spurs big off-season acquisition, Tobias Harris, who is nearing a return but there is no official timetable. The Spurs have stretches where they look like the best team in the league: Defending with ferocity, moving the ball, and getting easy buckets around the rim. Then the next quarter they fall in love with isolation basketball and things go cold, which happened too much against Minnesota on Halloween, but they got bailed out by 43 points from Victor “The Witcher” Wembanyama. Brett Siegel, Clutch Points — 4 (last week: 9) Victor Wembanyama was not about to let the San Antonio Spurs be below .500 for too long. Following a 0-2 start to the season, the Spurs have rattled off four straight wins and look like the team they were several months ago en route to the 2025 NBA Finals. Over their last four games, the Spurs have averaged 122.5 points per game, led by Wembanyama, who has averaged 32.8 points, 9.5 rebounds, and 4.3 blocks per game during this win streak. Wemby says he is aiming for the MVP award , and these are definitely MVP-like numbers. One of the more underappreciated players on this roster has been Julian Champagnie, who has shot 16-of-31, or 51.6 percent, from 3-point range in this span. He is shooting 47.6 percent from 3-point range on the season and proving to be one of the most impactful forwards off the bench in the entire NBA. Coming up Mon. 11/2 vs. Utah Jazz (7:30 PM CT) Wed. 11/4 vs. Dallas Mavericks (8:30 PM CT) Fri. 11/6 at Sacramento Kings (Emirates Cup, 9:00 PM CT) Sat. 11/7 at Portland Trail Blazers (9:00 PM CT) Prediction: 3-1 — I really want to go 4-0, but we need to see more consistency from the Spurs first. The Mavs with Cooper Flagg and noted Spurs killer Kyrie Irving, who both missed the first match-up, are a different animal, and strange things always happen in Portland, especially on the second night of a back-to-back. I believe the Spurs will ultimately split those games, but I’m more than ready to be proven wrong. Bonus content Not really Spurs related, but there has been so much drama in the NBA in the first two weeks alone — from injuries, to current and former teammate arguments, and scuffles — that it makes you appreciate the drama-free Spurs (outside of the first two games, of course). Here is a quick summary of all the craziness, in case you need catching up. i recapped all of the drama in the NBA this week like a reality TV show pic.twitter.com/kTYnwXqwwf — Molly Morrison (@mollyhannahm) November 2, 2026

teamStories.detailText: To the Victor goes the spoils … and that includes a 13-minute infomercial on CBS . In the first 60 Minutes profile of a Spur since David Robinson got the prime-time treatment in 1992 , millions of viewers got up close and personal with Victor Wembanyama Sunday night. Correspondent Jon Wertheim introduced the glowing feature by saying, “While (Wembanyama) may be best known for his height and length, it’s nothing compared to his depth.” Lauding Wemby’s “holy matrimony of size and skill,” Wertheim highlighted the remarkable on-court success of the franchise and its French centerpiece. But much of the profile focused on the characteristics that help Wembanyama transcend sports and become a human interest story for 60 Minutes’ mainstream audience. The feature focused on Wemby’s intentionality when it comes to training and taking care of his body and mind. That included, of course, his summer in China with Buddhist monks , his passion for chess, and his health-conscious affinity for walking around barefoot. At one point, Wertheim said, “You appreciate that, never mind athletes, not all people have your level of curiosity,” to which Wemby responded, “Yeah. It’s the defining trait of mine.” The segment featured plenty of the deep-thinking eloquence we’ve grown accustomed to, along with the supreme confidence we’re familiar with as well. During the interview, Wemby identified his 2025 battle with a blood clot as the trigger for taking off the filter. As we know, he’ll shoot straight on everything from his MVP worthiness to the political climate both here and in his home country. He said, “Life is so short, I don’t even wanna waste it being somebody else, you know?” These 13 minutes with Wemby certainly aren’t a waste for Spurs fans. teamStories.detailText: The 2026-27 NBA season was projected to be abnormally competitive, as previously rebuilding teams turned the corner and new draft lottery rules gave all 30 franchises an incentive to win . At the top of the standings , though, three juggernaut rosters towered above the rest: the Oklahoma City Thunder and San Antonio Spurs , who both won more than 60 games before clashing in a seven-game conference finals last season, and the defending champion New York Knicks , who reeled off arguably the most dominant stretch in NBA history en route to the title . Those three teams were excellent last season, and they returned 14 of their combined 15 starters this fall. So even as the rest of the league's floor rose, the highest ceilings still appeared to reside in New York City and the Southwest. But surprising developments have changed that narrative less than two weeks into the new season and challenged the triumvirate's hegemony atop the league. Most importantly, a wave of injuries to star players already has altered the league's most important races. Jump to a section: How title odds have shifted The injured stars so far Is the MVP race wide open? Scuffling preseason favorites Oklahoma City opened its season with a firm statement of intent, with 12-point wins over the Spurs and Nuggets -- possibly the Thunder's closest competition in the West. Then disaster struck . Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace both suffered potentially season-ending injuries in the same game, and Alex Caruso sprained his right ankle the following night. At the same time, Chet Holmgren suffered a patellar tendon tear in his right knee, which will sideline him for at least two months So Oklahoma City has played its past couple games without four of its top six players, to predictable results: a 24-point loss in Dallas followed by a 21-point loss in Houston. The Thunder were outscored in all eight quarters across those two defeats. The team will theoretically improve from their current doldrums once Caruso and Holmgren return, but the Thunder are in deep trouble on the perimeter without Williams and Wallace. They look far away from meaningful contention given their horrid spate of injuries. But Oklahoma City isn't the only preseason favorite with more concerns now than two weeks ago. The Knicks are 2-4 and needed two big comebacks against Detroit and Chicago just to pick up their two wins. And the Spurs started a comparatively better 4-2, but they've looked out of sorts against the toughest competition they've faced and needed overtime to beat the injury-wracked Jazz . It's very early, and those teams still have plenty of time to round into their best shape. But the title race already looks more open. According to preseason projections by ESPN's Basketball Power Index (BPI), the Thunder and Spurs combined for a 50% championship probability. Add in the Knicks at 8%, and BPI gave those three favorites a roughly three-fifths chance to win the title. Yet their combined odds have since fallen to just 38% , and that's with the assumption that Wallace and Holmgren return before the playoffs. Meanwhile, a series of second-tier contenders have started strong, which should increase their confidence that they can close the gap to the Thunder, Spurs and Knicks. The Rockets lead the way with a 5-1 record including wins over Oklahoma City and San Antonio . And in the Eastern Conference, the 76ers, Pistons and Celtics started a combined 16-3 -- meaning those three teams have fewer combined losses than the Knicks have by themselves. That trend also serves as an argument for teams with strong rosters and ample draft assets, such as Houston and Detroit, to seriously consider making in-season trades with an eye on the Finals. If the Thunder, Spurs and Knicks were all fully healthy and running roughshod over everyone in their paths, there might be some merit to the idea of keeping one's powder dry rather than making futile trades to try to catch the leading contenders. But if those teams still look more vulnerable than expected in a few months, the deadline could pack a more potent punch. Even more injuries Other prospective contenders have also borne the brunt of early-season injuries -- though none to the extent of Oklahoma City's nightmare. Players who have already missed multiple games this season include Williams, Wallace, Caruso, Holmgren, Coby White , Kon Knueppel , Cameron Johnson , Jalen Duren , Alperen Sengun , Tyrese Haliburton , Ivica Zubac , Anthony Edwards , Paolo Banchero , Jalen Suggs , Kawhi Leonard and Jaren Jackson Jr . That's more than a full roster's worth of stars (or star role players) who have suffered injuries within the first two weeks of the new season. Discussion around the league generally points to increased pace and stress on the body as a reason for these injuries, while understanding that they're a mix of soft tissue problems and flukes -- like the collisions that sidelined Williams and Wallace. It's also clear that there are no quick fixes. The NBA isn't slowing down, and more radical proposals that would change the sport to reduce wear and tear -- from a shorter schedule to 40-minute games -- are equally unlikely to happen any time soon. The injury issue is a figurative pain point for the league and a literal pain point for the players who keep getting hurt. A (potentially) wide-open MVP race Looking ahead to the remaining five months of the regular season, it's not just the title race that has opened to new challengers. The MVP race could also devolve into a free-for-all with one more injury. The two most recent MVPs , who have finished first and second in the voting in some order three years running, have scuffled to start this season, with numbers well below their recent norms. Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and Nikola Jokic perennially rank among the most productive, efficient stars in the league, but both have looked surprisingly mortal in the early going. Put another way, Jokic and Gilgeous-Alexander finished first and second in player efficiency rating in each of the past two seasons, and they ranked first and third in 2023-24. Jokic has led the league in PER six years in a row. Now, Jokic ranks 24th and Gilgeous-Alexander is 16th among qualified players in PER two weeks into this season. Of course, these comparisons come after a very small sample of play -- but even then, the stars' relative struggles are unusual. Jokic, for instance, just completed his worst five-game stretch (as measured by box plus-minus) at any point in the season since 2020, before he won his first MVP. For Gilgeous-Alexander, the Thunder's injury issues could counterintuitively give him a better chance to win his third straight MVP. Two-time winners are typically penalized -- if only unconsciously -- by voter fatigue, as no player has won three in a row since Larry Bird in the mid-'80s. However, if Gilgeous-Alexander can keep the Thunder near the top of the Western Conference standings and post his typically exemplary statistics without as much help from teammates, then he'd have a narrative boost to overcome that bias. Yet if he and Jokic don't live up to the incredibly high standards they set while winning multiple MVPs apiece, then it seems far-fetched to think that either could claim another trophy this season. That leaves Victor Wembanyama as the clear favorite, and betting odds reflect that status. He's responded by playing at an MVP level so far. But remember, Wembanyama reached only the bare minimum number of games to qualify for awards last season, and he missed out in 2024-25. If he falls short of 65 games again, he could leave behind a truly wide-open race, with a whole host of viable second-tier candidates suddenly receiving real MVP consideration. Could Luka Doncic finally receive his long-awaited MVP moment? Could Cade Cunningham , Jayson Tatum or Jalen Brunson become the first Eastern Conference perimeter players to win MVP since LeBron James in Miami? Could 19-year-old Cooper Flagg make a play at an historic award? (The answer is yes if he keeps dominating like he did in his first five games.) The result is a season that brims with tremendous possibility -- even more than already seemed to be the case when the new year tipped off in October.

teamStories.title: Open Thread: Inside the NBA’s Ernie Johnson announces this is his final season
teamStories.summary: After 37 years, the sportscaster is retiring
teamStories.detailText: Apr 3, 2026; Indianapolis, IN, USA; Ernie Johnson looks on during a practice session ahead of the Final Four of the men's 2026 NCAA Tournament at Lucas Oil Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Bob Donnan-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect For thirty-eight years, Inside the NBA has been a staple of basketball analysis. In its premiere season, the show had no dedicated host. The following year, sideline reporter Ernie Johnson claimed the position as the show’s host, a role he has maintain ever since. Last week, the emcee and ringleader tasked with managing the personalities of Shaquille O’Neal, Charles Barkley, and Kenny “The Jet” Smith disclosed that the 2026-2027 season will be his last with the show. The announcement was immediately met with sorrow from the trio of retired players for which he’s shared the broadcast over the years. As Ernie Johnson announced his final season, Charles Barkley’s emotional on-air struggle to thank him underscores the deep respect earned by Johnson’s resilience and selfless anchoring style. pic.twitter.com/m6bRWOR43F — SpursRΞPORTΞR (@SpursReporter) October 29, 2026 Johnson began his broadcasting career while attending the University of Georgia. A year after graduating, he worked as a newscaster in Macon, Georgia. Two years later he moved to South Carolina on general assignment, eventually picking up sports on the weekend. From 1993-1996, Johnson called Atalanta Braves games alongside his father, a 1950s Major League pitcher and Braves play-by-play announcer from 1962-1999. But E.J.’s bread-and-butter has been at the helm of Inside the NBA for over three decades. The steady hand, the voice of reason, and the man who has attempted for literally thousands of episodes to keep the train on the tracks. The show known for its chemistry and hijinks, highs and lows, and which, at times, seems to be less about basketball and more about the moment has engulfed the zeitgeist and become a staple of basketball. Whether it’s the analysis, the banter, sense of humor (Charles Barkley picks on San Antonio as a town quite a bit), or political commentary (Kenny Smith walked off the set in response to the shooting of Jacob Blake), Inside the NBA has embraced fans worldwide. When the show lost its broadcasting rights, Barkley walked away from an estimated $100 million to stay, saving the jobs of production and behind-the-scenes staff at Turner. In 2025, rather than being cancelled, Inside the NBA transitioned to ESPN and ABC while continuing to be produced by TNT Sports with the original crew. The show has survived the slings and arrows. But one thing is for sure — once Ernie Johnson unplugs his microphone it will never be the same. Welcome to the Thread. Join in the conversation, start your own discussion, and share your thoughts. This is the Spurs community, your Spurs community. Thanks for being here. Our community guidelines apply which should remind everyone to be cool, avoid personal attacks, not to troll and to watch the language.
