teamStories.detailText: The San Antonio Spurs have won four straight games after a disappointing start to the season. One of those wins recently came in overtime against the Utah Jazz. Now, just a half a week later, the Spurs will rematch the young Jazz at home, looking to extend their winning streak to five games. The last game against the Jazz was a back-and-forth affair, with the Spurs starting slow and finishing strong in overtime. Utah got some stellar performances from their young guards, while San Antonio needed a 36-point, 14-rebound Victor Wembanyama performance to get the job done. The Jazz played that game without one of their best players, Lauri Markkanen, but will get him back on Monday night. Markkanen is averaging 15.4 points per game this season. San Antonio is coming off a convincing Halloween win over a shorthanded Minnesota Timberwolves squad, developing an early-season rhythm. While the Jazz are just 1-5 to start the season, they’ll pose a real challenge to San Antonio. The Spurs will need to bring their A-game if they want to keep up momentum heading into November. San Antonio Spurs (4-2) vs. Utah Jazz (1-5) November 2nd, 2026 | 7:30 PM CT Watch: DAZN | Listen: WOAI (1200 AM) Spurs Injuries : Tobias Harris – Out (calf), Jayden Quaintance – Out (knee) Jazz Injuries: Trey Alexander – Out (G League), Kobe Bufkin – Out (G League), Harrison Ingram – Out (G League), Jaren Jackson Jr. – Out (knee), Jusuf Nurkic – Out (foot) What to watch for: Wembanyama and Fox San Antonio has gotten great production from their two best players to start the season. The San Antonio Spurs are +96 points in 213 possessions with the duo on the court this year. They are -17 points when they sit. Fox and Wembanyama have found great synergy in the pick-and-roll, where Fox has used Wembanyama’s gravity to find openings in the mid-range, where he is hitting shots at a high percentage. Wembanyama has become more committed to rolling to the basket, creating easier opportunities when opponents switch. The Jazz were great in the last game at staying disciplined and fighting through screens to keep their big man contesting Wembanyama lobs. Fox and Wembanyama finding an edge will be crucial to the Spurs’ success. Slowing down Keyonte George George lit up the Spurs for 31 points on 11-27 shooting from the field in their last contest. He especially had it going early, as he hit several pull-up jumpers. San Antonio will need to find a way to slow the opposing guard down, whether with a one-on-one defender like Stephon Castle or a team scheme that forces George to take difficult shots inside of the three-point arc. In general, the Spurs will need to get out to Utah’s shooters, who can get hot quickly. Getting to the rim The Jazz are thin in the front court thanks to injuries to Jaren Jackson Jr. and Jusuf Nurkic. Jaxson Hayes, Markkanen, and Mo Bamba are leading Utah’s big man rotation. None of those big men are particularly elite at defending the paint. Wembanyama exposed this in the last game between these teams. San Antonio will need to find a way to get downhill against the Jazz and challenge their limited front-court depth.

teamStories.summary: The Spurs have rallied after losing their first two games of the season, rattling off four wins in a row. Among the areas that still need improvement is […]
teamStories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO, TX - OCTOBER 27: Luke Kornet #7 of the San Antonio Spurs handles the ball during the game against the Sacramento Kings on October 27, 2026 at the Frost Bank Center in San Antonio, Texas. NOTE TO USER: User expressly acknowledges and agrees that, by downloading and or using this photograph, user is consenting to the terms and conditions of the Getty Images License Agreement. Mandatory Copyright Notice: Copyright 2026 NBAE (Photos by Michael Gonzales/NBAE via Getty Images) | NBAE via Getty Images The Spurs have rallied after losing their first two games of the season, rattling off four wins in a row. They are starting to round into form while still having room for growth, looking like the contender their talent suggests they can be, through ups and downs. Among the areas that still need improvement is the play of the second unit. And among the reserves, Luke Kornet has been getting a lot of scrutiny, as he hasn’t bounced back to the form he showed last year and now has an exciting rookie behind him who has looked productive in limited minutes. In the Spurs’ latest win against the shorthanded Timberwolves, Kornet looked good, but his solid performance won’t completely get him off the hook from those who might want to see Tarris Reed Jr. get a chance to fight for the backup center spot as soon as possible. While the rookie should get his opportunity if Kornet continues to struggle, for now, being patient with the veteran seems like the right move. The offense is terrible with Kornet on the floor, but it’s not necessarily his fault It’s always tricky to put too much stock in advanced numbers with so few minutes to go by, but they are not kind to Kornet. The Spurs score just 100.5 points per 100 possessions when he’s on the floor, a ghastly number. His limitations on that end are well-known, and it doesn’t feel like he has developed any other tools, such as a floater, to change that. His strengths, however, are also clear and are not insignificant. Kornet is a good screener. In just 14.6 minutes a game, he’s averaging 2.7 screen assists, the 18th most in the league, and those screen assists are resulting in six points per game, the 25th-best mark in the league. Now, screen assists tend to be higher for limited role-playing centers who don’t get the ball back after initially freeing their ball-handler. There’s a reason why Victor Wembanyama averages fewer despite playing over twice as many minutes as Luke: Wemby screens, then the guards find him, and Wemby scores. The Alien leads the league in plays finished as the pick-and-roll dive man, which makes sense. Luke can’t do that. Context is important. Still, the screening is good, as anyone who has watched Kornet play can attest to, and while he doesn’t finish after a pass, he has another skill that he can use after setting them: grabbing offensive rebounds. His offensive rebound percentage has dipped slightly from last year, but it’s still very good. So if Kornet is doing his job on offense, why are the Spurs struggling to score when he’s on the floor? First, he’s currently posting an uncharacteristically high turnover percentage that is bound to come down significantly. He’s been fumbling passes and losing offensive boards, and while he’ll always do that to an extent, there’s simply no way he continues to do it at the pace his done it so far. If he somehow does, he won’t only be out of the rotation but out of the league soon. Second, the Spurs are shooting very few threes per possession when he’s on the floor (in part explained by the fact that Kornet doesn’t take them) while also connecting on just 33.2 percent of them. When Kornet is off the floor, that number climbs to 35.9 on more attempts. There’s a decent chance the Spurs simply start shooting better when Kornet is on the floor, and there’s no way his turnover percentage remains as high, considering his usage. Mitch Johnson should try giving Reed Jr. some minutes whenever possible, but prematurely giving up on Kornet because of the offense’s struggles would be unwise. The defense’s big problem seems more related to lineups than whoever plays center If the offense was the only issue, there would be little reason to demote Kornet. The problem is, the Spurs have also been horrendous on defense, both by the numbers and the eye test, when Wembanyama is not on the floor. A big decline in efficiency is obviously expected when the best defender of his generation rests, but so far, it’s been precipitous. No one expects Kornet to match Wemby, but a 22-point swing in points allowed per 100 possessions is simply too big and not even close to the more reasonable seven-point swing from last season. Even though the numbers should normalize with more minutes, Kornet just hasn’t looked good out there. Still, he’s rebounding at a decent level, but the Spurs are allowing a lot of second-chance points when he’s on the floor anyway, and while his allowing a very low percentage at the rim when he’s the closest defender, other teams’ points in the paint have been high. What those numbers suggest, then, is that maybe the issue is not necessarily Kornet but the teammates he shares the floor with. Mitch Johnson explicitly said that the struggles of units featuring Kornet have to be seen as collective instead of individual , because there are four other players out there with him, and he’s right. Kornet has shared the floor very often with Keldon Johnson, a poor defender, and those minutes have been horrendous. In lineups that feature more of the starters (and once again, the numbers need to be taken with a grain of salt), the defensive rating is much lower. Most other Spurs are also used to playing a very aggressive style of perimeter defense when Wembanyama is around, and Kornet simply can’t cover as much space as Wemby does or erase or deter as many shots at the rim once the ball handler gets past the first line of defense. The new lineups developing familiarity should help. As with the offense, it seems like Kornet, while partially responsible, is not individually to blame for the bad results. He has not been as good as he was last season so far, but a combination of issues involving the lineups he’s in and some seemingly aberrant numbers that should, on paper, get back to normal with a bigger sample size are likely the biggest reasons for the poor performance of the bench units. Tarris Reed Jr. could be a better option, but it’s far from a certainty Whether Kornet can go back to being the version of himself from last season, which was a perfectly good backup in most matchups, is irrelevant if there’s a better option waiting in the wings. If Reed Jr. is simply a superior player, he should be getting Kornet’s minutes. There are two issues with any claim that he is, however. The first is that he’s untested, which can only be solved by playing him, but the second has to do with the limitations that Reed has displayed so far. The rookie has shown some touch around the rim and, perhaps more importantly, more ambition in terms of finishing plays when he gets the ball in the paint than the more passive Kornet, but they both share strengths and weaknesses. Kornet is likely the better screener while Reed Jr. is almost certainly a better offensive rebounder, but neither spaces the floor either horizontally, as both have limited range, or vertically, as they are both big but not explosive. Passing has never been Reed Jr.’s biggest strength, so he won’t likely offer another dimension to the offense in that area, at least as a rookie. Defensively, both Reed Jr. and Kornet are only suited for drop coverage, since their foot speed is limited, and both are at their best close to the rim. While the rookie might offer more energy, that could be a plus when it becomes contagious, but it can also be a negative if it results in chaos. Kornet is likely a better steadying force in that regard due to his experience, while once again Reed Jr. has an edge in rebounding. Both have similarly good cases for the non-Wemby minutes. If Kornet continues to struggle, Mitch Johnson should absolutely give the rookie some more playing time, but Reed Jr. shouldn’t be considered an automatic upgrade who will solve every issue. Especially if the coaching staff’s only change is swapping the two in the rotation instead of addressing the other problems with the non-Wembanyama units. Kornet is far from untouchable, and he might lose his spot eventually. But there’s no rush to make a change now, as the season is long and the Spurs are clearly still a work in progress, trying to figure out more important things than their backup center situation.

teamStories.summary: Victor Wembanyama launched a career-high 34 shots for a season-high 43 points to propel the Spurs to a 121-111 win over the Timberwolves.
teamStories.detailText: SAN ANTONIO -- Spurs star Victor Wembanyama launched a career-high 34 shots for a season-high 43 points Saturday to propel San Antonio to a 121-111 win over the Timberwolves . "When he plays with his teammates, it really causes a problem for the other team, whether that's spacing, handling the basketball, playing two-man game or three-man game," Spurs coach Mitch Johnson said. "The best players in this league, when they play with their teammates, it's damn near impossible at times [to stop]. You've got to just choose how they beat you. He's made some fine improvement in a short amount of time." Wembanyama's performance marked the first time the Spurs emerged victorious on a night the Frenchman finished with 30 attempts or more. The 22-year-old also contributed five blocks to become the first Spurs player since David Robinson (1996) to rack up at least 40 points and five blocks in a game and the first player in the NBA since Joel Embiid (2022) to accomplish the feat. San Antonio fell short the two previous times Wembanyama hoisted 30 shots or more. He attempted 31 shots on Christmas Day of his second NBA season (2024) to finish with 42 points in a 117-114 loss to the New York Knicks . Four days later, Wembanyama finished with 30 attempts in a 112-110 loss to the Timberwolves. "He's just so dominant," said second-year guard Dylan Harper , who notched a regular-season career-high 25 points on 9-of-17 shooting. "When he puts his imprint on the game, he's unstoppable. He did that tonight from the jump to the end of the game." Wembanyama's shot diet looked different too. He nailed a corner 3-pointer with 2:40 remaining for his final bucket to extend San Antonio's lead to 118-107. Wembanyama would fire up eight 3-pointers on the night, knocking down three of them. But 12 of Wembanyama's 14 other baskets came from distances of two feet or fewer, including four alley-oops and four dunks. Wembanyama mentioned after struggling in San Antonio's season-opening loss to the Oklahoma City Thunder that he needed "to go back to playing the basketball I like." By the 5:23 mark of the third quarter, the "WemVP" chants started raining down on Wembanyama as he took a pair of foul shots. "It's like pattern recognition," he said. "The brain, after so many games, literally hundreds of games now in the NBA, knows what kind of game to go towards to have fun. Because whenever we don't score, it's like negative feedback. Whenever we score, we get good results, positive feedback for the brain. Over time, you recognize patterns, and you err towards those patterns. There's always ups and downs, but we're turning in the right direction." San Antonio's four-guard starting lineup featuring Wembanyama, De'Aaron Fox , Stephon Castle , Devin Vassell and Harper continues to make progress. Wembanyama, Fox and Harper combined for 90 points as the Spurs won the rebounding battle 49-38. Castle finished with four assists and a steal despite fighting through a migraine headache during his 22 minutes on the floor. Wembanyama declined to divulge what's exactly behind his increased comfort level lately, saying "it will help my opponents" to openly discuss. The Frenchman has dropped 36 and 43 points in his last two outings, as the Spurs extended their winning streak to four games. On Saturday, San Antonio faced a depleted Timberwolves team missing star guard Anthony Edwards (knee). LaMelo Ball played only 20 minutes, and he picked up four fouls in the first half before fouling out with 3:43 remaining.

stories.title: Shane Steichen sticking with Daniel Jones as Colts' QB1 for Week 9 vs. Cowboys
stories.summary: Daniel Jones will remain the Colts' starting quarterback for Sunday's game against the Cowboys.
stories.detailText: INDIANAPOLIS -- Daniel Jones remains the Colts ' QB1. Coach Shane Steichen on Monday said Jones will remain the Colts' starting quarterback for the team's Week 9 game against the Dallas Cowboys despite leaving the door open to a change after the Colts' 42-7 loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars on Sunday. Jones completed 19 of 28 passes for 144 yards against Jacksonville (5.1 yards per attempt), throwing two more interceptions to raise his season total to nine picks. One of the interceptions came on a dropped pass by tight end Tyler Warren , resulting in a pick-six touchdown for the Jaguars. The Colts' offense ranks among the worst in the NFL in many major categories, including offensive expected points added (31st). Personally, Jones has ranked as one of the worst quarterbacks this season in QBR. His 39.6 QBR is the second worst he has produced in his eight seasons. But Steichen warned that the issues plaguing the Colts' offense are bigger than Jones. "Evaluating the tape, looking back at it, some things he could do better, some things that we need to help him with moving forward," Steichen said. "But I do feel that Daniel gives us the best chance to win right now." After Sunday's game, Steichen for the first time this season offered a different answer when asked about Jones' status. Asked about Jones' status in his postgame news conference, Steichen said, "I'm going to evaluate everything, every position going forward." Asked on Monday to elaborate on his decision to stick with Jones, Steichen suggested performance at other positions has played a role in Jones' struggles. "Obviously, the quarterback takes the brunt of it all," Steichen said. "As we know, that's what the quarterback signs up for. And it's not all on him, right? It's everything. It's all encompassing. It's everyone doing their job, being on the same page, the route discipline, the route detail, the blocking, the protections -- all those things tie into it." Jones was sacked four times in the game and the Jaguars registered 10 quarterback hits. Colts backup Anthony Richardson Sr ., who last started a game for Indianapolis in December 2024, relieved Jones late in the game with the Colts down 35 points. Steichen said at the time the decision was prompted by the score, not indicative of any larger decision.

stories.title: Brandon Aiyuk hires Drew Rosenhaus as agent, eyes return to NFL
stories.summary: Brandon Aiyuk has hired agent Drew Rosenhaus, who told ESPN's Adam Schefter that he is "working on getting him back to work and playing again in the NFL."
stories.detailText: SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- Estranged San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk has hired Drew Rosenhaus to represent him, the agent told ESPN's Adam Schefter on Monday. Rosenhaus told Schefter that he is "working on getting [Aiyuk] back to work and playing again in the NFL." Aiyuk has not played in an NFL game since Oct. 20, 2024, against the Kansas City Chiefs , when he tore the ACL, MCL and meniscus in his right knee. For most of the time since, Aiyuk and the Niners have been at odds. The team placed Aiyuk on the reserve/left squad list in December after Aiyuk stopped showing up at the team facility. That came on the heels of the Niners voiding roughly $27 million in guaranteed money on Aiyuk's contract in July 2025 because he did not do the requisite rehab sessions and check-ins with the team during that offseason. When Aiyuk did not report for training camp in July, he reverted to the reserve/did not report list. For Aiyuk to play again, he must first apply for reinstatement with the NFL. If he does that, the Niners will then need to decide what to do with his rights. San Francisco has tried unsuccessfully to trade Aiyuk in the past, but if he's reinstated, the more likely outcome would be the team releasing him. Either way, 49ers general manager John Lynch and coach Kyle Shanahan have made it repeatedly clear that Aiyuk has played his last snap in San Francisco. Most recently, despite myriad injuries at receiver, when Shanahan was asked if he would reconsider a reunion with Aiyuk in September, Shanahan said, simply, "no." Over the summer, Aiyuk took to social media multiple times to voice his displeasure with the Niners and attempted to goad them into releasing him while also saying he wouldn't "do business" with the team at all. On multiple occasions, Aiyuk also implied or openly suggested that he wanted to join the Washington Commanders to play with quarterback Jayden Daniels , with whom he had formed a friendship in their shared time together at Arizona State. It's unclear whether landing in Washington is even an option still with the Commanders having signed veteran Stefon Diggs and having other wideouts they're hoping to develop. As it stands, Aiyuk's status on the reserve/did not report list means the Niners are not paying him and he does not count against their roster. The Niners originally selected Aiyuk, 28, with the No. 25 pick in the 2020 NFL draft. Before his knee injury, Aiyuk had emerged as one of the NFL's most productive wideouts. He had 75 catches for 1,342 yards and seven touchdowns on his way to second-team All-Pro honors in 2023.

stories.title: Vikings uncertain of QB Kyler Murray's status vs. Bills due to sore hamstring
stories.summary: Vikings QB Kyler Murray's status for the Week 9 game against the Bills is uncertain due to a sore hamstring.
stories.detailText: EAGAN, Minn. -- Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray 's hamstring was sore enough Monday that the team is uncertain whether he will be available for the team's Week 9 game against the Buffalo Bills . A day after Murray struggled in a 19-15 loss to the Detroit Lions , coach Kevin O'Connell said that Murray was going through a "full eval" Monday and that he expected additional updates from the Vikings' medical staff during the early part of the week. Asked if he thought the injury was serious enough to prevent Murray from playing against the Bills, O'Connell said: "I don't think we're there yet. It's still early enough that I'll continue to get updates." If Murray can't play, backup Carson Wentz would make his second start of the season. O'Connell, however, made clear that he is not considering benching Murray for performance reasons. Through his first six starts with the Vikings, Murray ranks No. 26 among 30 qualified quarterbacks in QBR. But when asked if Murray would continue to be his starter when healthy, O'Connell said: "Yes." Murray missed receiver Justin Jefferson on multiple opportunities for big plays against the Lions, and O'Connell dissected many of them during his postgame news conference in Detroit . On Monday, O'Connell spoke as if he is still moving forward with the ongoing project of getting Murray acclimated to the offense -- and vice versa -- nearly eight months after signing him as a free agent. "I think it's just continuing to build that rapport of the plans, the comfort level," O'Connell said, "[and] continuing to implore some input from him on things he likes and things [where] we carve it and make it even cleaner and better for him -- so that we do get some of that comfort where he'll throw things with anticipation and we get the look for a play and we all know it's coming and we see the pitch and catch there."

stories.title: Chiefs' Reid says he didn't bench OL Suamataia as punishment
stories.summary: Chiefs coach Andy Reid explained Monday that his decision to bench left guard Kingsley Suamataia for Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos was not punishment toward the three-year player.
stories.detailText: DENVER -- Chiefs coach Andy Reid explained Monday that his decision to bench left guard Kingsley Suamataia for Sunday's game against the Denver Broncos was not punishment toward the three-year player. "This is just between Kingsley and I," Reid said, reiterating what he said after the Chiefs' 28-24 loss. "It's not something that's earth shattering. I'll just keep it there." Prior to Sunday's game, Suamataia was a full participant in the Chiefs' three practices last week and wasn't on the team's injury report. But during the team's pregame warmup, backup guard Mike Caliendo , a four-year veteran, took most of the reps at left guard with the rest of the starting offensive line. Caliendo played all 69 of the Chiefs' offensive snaps while Suamataia was on the field for just five snaps on special teams. Without Suamataia, the 2024 second-round pick, the Chiefs didn't have much success running the ball against the Broncos. Running back Kenneth Walker III finished with just 69 rushing yards on 21 attempts. Caliendo also struggled in pass protection on the final snap of the game -- a fourth-and-goal from the Broncos' 6-yard line -- in losing to defensive end Malcolm Roach , who sacked quarterback Patrick Mahomes . "I didn't say it was punishment, ever," Reid said of Suamataia being benched in Week 4 against the Las Vegas Raiders . "This was just between Kingsley and I working some things out here. This isn't punishment. I'll leave it at that." Despite being benched twice this season, Suamataia is likely to return to the starting lineup for the Chiefs' next game against the New York Jets . "He's family," tight end Travis Kelce said of Suamataia after the game. "Everybody has their own road. We love Kingsley, and we think he's a hell of a player. At this time, I'm not even sure what the scenario is. I'm rolling with whoever we've got in that game. "I'm sure Kingsley is drooling, trying to get back out there. We just have to find ways to win games, and Kingsley is one of those guys that will be ready next time his number is called."

stories.title: Chargers Week 8 PFF Grades: Herbert struggles despite great protection up front vs. Rams
stories.summary: Joe Alt was nearly elite in pass protection against the Rams while rookie Isas Waxter was a standout on defense.
stories.detailText: INGLEWOOD, CA - NOVEMBER 01: Joe Alt #76 of the Los Angeles Chargers guards Kam Curl #3 of the Los Angeles Rams during an NFL game between the Los Angeles Chargers and the Los Angeles Rams on November 1, 2026, at SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California. (Photo by Greg Fiore/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Justin Herbert turned the ball over in the seventh consecutive game to begin the 2026 season. He ended with a pair of interceptions thrown and another fumble that luckily was knocked out of bounds before the Rams could secure it. Most days, it’s easy to turn around and blame the offensive line who normally puts up an underwhelming performance in pass protection. That wasn’t the case in Week Eight as nearly the entire front five had a decent to great day protecting Herbert. The defense unsurprisingly had some standouts. Holding the Rams to zero first downs through the game’s first 28 and a half minutes is something to be very proud of. Unfortunately the nine points score during that stretch of dominance was nowhere near enough to put the game away. Let’s go ahead and check out the grades from Sunday. Offense Best OT Joe Alt – 77.7 TE Oronde Gadsden II – 74.4 OT Travis Burke – 69.4 WR Tre’ Harris – 66.1 WR Quentin Johnston – 63.1 Alt remains one of the top offensive tackles in the NFL and that didn’t change after missing two games with a nek injury. He returned to be the top player on the offense, posting a pass block grade of 89.9 which fell a hair short of an elite mark. Gadsden had season-high 52 yards receiving against the Rams on five receptions, also tying his previous season high. With eight catches on 10 targets over the past two games, the hope is that McDaniel keeps pushing to get Gadsden back to his rookie season form where he was a surprising standout. The rookie Burke remains one of the Chargers’ best offensive players despite being forced into a starting role much sooner than he likely expected. Behind both Alt and Rashawn Slater, Burke is actually the team’s third-highest-graded player on the year. He had a team-high 67.5 run block grade against the Rams. In his first game back from injury, Harris was the team’s highest-graded wideout after catching three passes for 31 yards. He remains the best run-blocking wideout for the Chargers. Johnston also caught all four of his targets for 37 yards. Worst FB Scott Matlock – 31.9 RB Omarion Hampton – 47.2 OG Cole Strange – 48.6 QB Justin Herbert – 50.2 WR Ladd McConkey – 51.0 After a strong return to the field following his IR stint, Matlock had a rough outing against the Rams where he earned a porous 38.5 as a run blocker and was flagged for a penalty. Hampton’s 30.5 receiving grade sunk his overall mark. He had a very strong 74.9 in pass protection, though. Strange is on pace for the worst overall season grade of his career. His 39.5 pass block grade on the year remains atrocious and he continues to be one of the bottom five Chargers players week-in and week-out. Herbert threw two more interceptions and only grew his league-leading total to 10. McConkey dropped one of the first passes thrown his way on Sunday and his stat line (4-86) would have looked a lot better if he didn’t luck into catching the Hail Mary attempt at the end of the first half (54 yards). Defense Best CB Isas Waxter – 89.0 S R.J. Mickens – 84.2 LB Troy Dye – 82.8 LB Del’Shawn Phillips – 79.8 DT Justin Eboigbe – 73.7 Look at the rookie Waxter go! He was the highest-graded player not only on defense, but the entire Chargers team. He posted an 89.9 in coverage. His 79.6 tackling grade was also third best on the team. This was Mickens’ best game of the year, as well. His 85.6 in tackling topped the team and his 75.1 in coverage was fifth best. Despite playing very few snaps each week, Dye has been impactful. His 80.8 in coverage was second on the team while his 76.9 in tackling was fourth best. Eboigbe was one of the team’s best run defenders (74.5 in run defense) and was sixth in tackling (71.2). Worst LB Daiyan Henley – 27.7 DT Dalvin Tomlinson – 29.8 DT Jamaree Caldwell – 47.4 S Elijah Molden – 53.3 DT Nick Barrett – 55.1 Henley had a very rough outing against the Rams. He was put on his butt more than once and struggled mightily in coverage (27.2). He allowed all four targets his way to be completed and missed a tackle. Tomlinson posted the team’s worst run defense grade with a 29.9. Molden was put one-on-one with a running back in the open field multiple times on Sunday. It never ended well for him and that’s reflected in his run defense (33.0) and tackling (24.6) grades.

stories.title: Packers sticking with RB Josh Jacobs despite latest abuse allegations
stories.summary: Packers coach Matt LaFleur says the team is sticking with RB Josh Jacobs despite new allegations of abuse levied by multiple women in addition to a May incident that led to his arrest.
stories.detailText: GREEN BAY, Wis. -- The Green Bay Packers are sticking with running back Josh Jacobs despite the additional allegations of physical and verbal abuse against multiple women several years before the May incident that led to his arrest . The Packers became aware of the previous allegations only after records were released last week. Those records indicated three women came forward after Jacobs' arrest earlier this year. "We're going to allow the NFL to do its process, but I would anticipate him being a member of us moving forward," Packers coach Matt LaFleur said Monday. "That's really all I have to speak on." Jacobs' attorneys said the previous claims are "unsupported and stale allegations" in a statement released on Sunday , two days after the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department in Wisconsin released records related to his May 23 arrest after an incident with a woman at his home near Green Bay. Jacobs pleaded no contest to two misdemeanor charges in September . He was convicted of battery and fined $1,000 and agreed to a deferred judgment agreement on a charge of damage to property. The Packers have continued to support Jacobs throughout the process and allowed him to return to the field in Week 7 after he was taken off the NFL's commissioner exempt list. Jacobs has played in the last two games, although the NFL has not closed its investigation. Jacobs' six games on the exempt list would count toward any suspension that might be forthcoming. "Like I said, I'm not going to get into that up here right now," LaFleur said when asked why they're standing by Jacobs. "We'll just let the process play out." LaFleur said he talked with Jacobs about his touchdown celebration against the Carolina Panthers on Thursday night, when Jacobs put his hands behind his back. He said after the game it was an ode to the gospel song "Break Every Chain" and had nothing to do with anything related to his legal case. "I know he had his explanation, and I wasn't even aware of what happened until I saw the tape," LaFleur said. "But we had a conversation about that, and I'm going to keep the conversation between him and I, and you know, we're going to move forward." The Packers have the NFL's worst rushing offense, and Jacobs' return hasn't changed that. In two games, Jacobs has 32 carries for 75 yards and one rushing touchdown plus 11 catches for 68 yards and two receiving touchdowns.

stories.title: 3 new trade targets for the 49ers at receiver
stories.summary: Here are three names for the 49ers to target after Sunday’s games
stories.detailText: (Photo by Chris Arjoon/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images). | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images The San Francisco 49ers are working the phones for receiver help. According to Jay Glazer, the 49ers had a deal in place with the Minnesota Vikings to bring back receiver Jauan Jennings, which was ultimately nixed by Jennings himself. The good news is the 49ers are looking to add receiver help. The bad news is they might be aiming very low by targeting Jennings. The trades have slowed down, and that’s understandable, as Sunday’s games would help reveal teams who are now sellers. Through eight weeks, the sample size is good enough for teams to be truthful with themselves about the outlook for 2026. Yes, that means you, Los Angeles Chargers. Sunday’s games have helped add potential targets at wide receiver. Let’s look at three new names for the 49ers to target. Rashod Bateman, Baltimore With Baltimore looking at a lost season with the potential season-ending injury to Lamar Jackson, the Ravens have to consider moving players for draft capital. Zay Flowers is there to stay, and the Ravens drafted Ja’Kobi Lane and Elijah Sarratt. Bateman signed a three-year extension worth $36.75 million. $16.5 million was guaranteed at signing, with another $3.5 million guaranteed. With only 19 catches this season, Bateman is an afterthought in the Ravens’ offense. Better days aren’t ahead if Snoop Huntley or the emergency third QB has to finish the season. As a separator, Bateman holds a 1.42 separation score against man coverage (25th in the NFL) and a 1.79 separation score against zone. Perfect low-risk, high-reward move at the deadline. Elic Ayomanor, Tennessee The Titans are going nowhere fast, and the future is built around Carnell Tate, with the chance of landing Jeremiah Smith in the draft. Ayomanor is 6’2” and the perfect addition for Purdy and his affinity for taller receivers. Ayomanor has just 13 catches for 211 yards and a touchdown on the season. The 49ers did scout him at his pro days, and they would have control over the young receiver moving forward. John Lynch and the front office should return to Ayomanor and call Robert Saleh and the Titans about his potential price. Ayomanor would raise the floor of the receiver room and improve the depth. Malik Washington, Miami Now, stay with me here. Washington is more of a weapon, like Deebo Samuel, but the young receiver has shown juice, and his speed should be coveted. The Dolphins spent two draft picks on Caleb Douglas and Chris Bell, and the team is rightfully excited about both players. Washington scored on Sunday and has a total of 31 catches, 329 yards, and a touchdown. Washington is more of a complementary piece, which only works in tandem with Mike Evans, but his speed and YAC ability could boost the receiver room. Miami may not look to move him, but the sixth-round pick should receive some attention, and the 49ers should gauge his price.

stories.title: Packers expect Parsons at practice 'sometime this week'
stories.summary: Packers defensive end Micah Parsons will practice this week for the first time since he tore the ACL and meniscus in his left knee on Dec. 14 of last year.
stories.detailText: GREEN BAY, Wis. -- Packers defensive end Micah Parsons will practice this week for the first time since he tore the ACL and meniscus in his left knee on Dec. 14 of last year. "That would be the intention," coach Matt LaFleur said Monday. "Again, it's going to be a process trying to get him back, but we're hopeful. It's going to be dependent upon the next couple days, but we're hopeful he'll be able to get out there sometime this week." The Packers' next practice is Wednesday. LaFleur said the team held a walk-through Monday after the players had the weekend off following last Thursday's win over the Carolina Panthers . Parsons continued to work with the trainers on Monday and was not part of the walk-through, LaFleur said. Parsons underwent surgery on Dec. 29 to repair his torn ACL and torn meniscus, which meant he would have a longer recovery than if it was just a standard ACL reconstruction. He remains on the physically unable to perform list. The Packers will have 21 days from when Parsons first practices before they have to add him to the 53-man roster. "If I had a bet on it, it's going to be more towards the longer end than the shorter end," LaFleur said. That means Parsons won't play Sunday against the New England Patriots and likely would not play in Week 10 against the Minnesota Vikings . The Packers have their bye in Week 11, which would set up Parsons' return for their Thanksgiving eve game against the Rams. "I would just say it's like everything around here is, it's pretty fluid in terms of how he responds and just the progress he's going to hopefully continue to make leading up to when he's available," LaFleur said. In his first season with the Packers, Parsons had 12.5 sacks and a league-high 64 pressures despite playing in just 14 games. The Packers gave up two first-round picks and Kenny Clark to acquire Parsons in a trade from the Cowboys in August 2025 and signed him to a four-year, $188 contract extension.

stories.title: Would Patriots DT Christian Barmore be an upgrade for the Giants?
stories.summary: He appears to be available, and the Giants are said to be looking for defensive tackle help. Could Barmore provide it?
stories.detailText: Christian Barmore | Getty Images The New York Giants need defensive tackle help. Badly, enough, in fact, that head coach John Harbaugh recently took the unusual step of calling Tenneessee Titans owner Amy Adams Strunk directly to find out if the Giants could get Jeffery Simmons. That, of course, did not happen. There are other fish in the defensive tackle sea, however, though none would be a prize the size of Simmons, who was dealt to the Chicago Bears for two first-round picks and a fourth-round pick. One defensive tackle who is apparently available, and might help the Giants, is Christian Barmore of the New England Patriots. According to Sports Illustrated NFL insider Albert Breer, the veteran defender “ could be had” by a willing trade partner , and the price to get him would be about a fourth-round draft pick. “My understanding is the price would be about a fourth-round pick, and he may be tradable because if you look at his contract, he’s making $13.3 million this year,” Breer said on NBC Sports Boston . “So you’d be taking on a prorated number off of that if you did trade for him. His numbers balloon after this year. …Those numbers aren’t guaranteed. “So, a team could wind up walking away from that if they did trade for him. But this is a player that very clearly is available. And if somebody’s willing to swing the Patriots a fourth-round pick, I think something could happen.” Should the Giants be interested in the 6-foot-5, 315-pound 27-year-old? Why it would work The price would not be that high. Even though Barmore is in the midst of a four-year, $84 million contract nothing beyond this season is guaranteed. So, if you don’t like what you see over the remainder of the year, moving on is not an issue. Barmore is a former second-round pick with 19 career sacks, so there is clearly talent there. If he plays well, maybe he could be a piece of the defensive line going forward. Why it wouldn’t work There is a reason why Barmore has been losing playing time in New England to former undrafted free agent and one-time Giant Cory Durden. His run defense has been atrocious. “He’s been used more as a situational pass rusher than the three-down impact player he’s being paid to be,” said Bernd Buchmasser of SB Nation’s Pats Pulpit . “He also was extended by the Patriots before Mike Vrabel arrived and had some off-the-field and medical issues. Rumor has it a mid-round pick could be the price.” In his seasons, Barmore has had a Pro Football Focus run defense grade above the 60.0 average score just one time. Last season, his run defense grade was a miserable 33.6. This year, it is 44.8. By PFF grade, the Giants are getting far better play from the much-maligned Darius Alexander (59.6). Barmore’s Pro Football and Sports Network Impact Scores aren’t any more encouraging. PFSN gives him a 90.3 pass-rushing score, No. 7 among defensive tackles. Run defense? His PFSN score is 68.3, 106th among defensive tackles. “I don’t think it’s [Barmore’s run defense] necessarily that he’s bad, but he’s better attacking upfield than controlling his gap, for example,” Buchmasser said. “I think if you have a big nose to occupy the 0/1-tech spot and line him up at 3T, he can certainly be a serviceable run defender; he was at times last year when the Pats had Khyiris Tonga available. They don’t have anybody like that at the moment, and therefore nobody to lift some pressure off of Barmore when he is asked to do early-down run work.” The Giants need defensive tackles who help the run defense, not add more questions to it.

stories.title: Brandon Aiyuk hires Drew Rosenhaus in attempt to get wideout 'back to work and playing again in the NFL'
stories.summary: Brandon Aiyuk hasn't played in an NFL game since 2024.
stories.detailText: It's been over two years since San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Brandon Aiyuk played in an NFL game. After sustaining an ACL and MCL injury during the 2024 season, Aiyuk was initially placed on the PUP list ahead of 2025. But his relationship with the 49ers deteriorated, leading Aiyuk to not appear in a game despite still being under contract with the team. Now the wideout is looking to change that. In an attempt to get back in the NFL, the 28-year-old Aiyuk hired agent Drew Rosenhaus, per multiple media reports. Rosenhaus told reporters he is tasked with "working on getting [Aiyuk] back to work and playing again in the NFL ." Aiyuk was previously represented by agent Ryan Williams, but reportedly fired him last November. Aiyuk blamed Williams for the issues between the wideout and the 49ers. In December, the 49ers placed Aiyuk on the reserve/left team list. He remains on there today. Months after firing Williams, Aiyuk was vocal on social media, often expressing a desire to join the Washington Commanders. Aiyuk and Commanders quarterback Jayden Daniels played together at Arizona State for one season. That trade never materialized. If Aiyuk is serious about returning to the NFL, his path forward is unclear. With his relationship with the 49ers ruined, the wideout would first likely need to establish his intent to play again. It's unclear, however, if Aiyuk would be willing to report to the team if the 49ers required it. It's also unclear how much interest teams have in Aiyuk. While he proved to be immensely talented in 2022 and 2023, he hasn't played in an NFL game in two seasons and spent the past offseason torpedoing his chances of a return to the 49ers. Given the injury questions and his personal baggage, Aiyuk might not draw much interest on the trade market. While the 49ers could use help at wide receiver due to the team's various injuries, it doesn't appear the team is willing to welcome Aiyuk back. When asked about that possibility in September, 49ers head coach Kyle Shanahan simply replied "no" when the option was discussed . Aiyuk is still under contract with the 49ers through the 2028 season. He signed a four-year, $120 million extension with the team in 2024, just months before his season-ending knee injury.

stories.title: Brandon Aiyuk hires new representation; aims to play in the NFL again
stories.summary: The 49ers still control Brandon Aiyuk’s rights
stories.detailText: Mandatory Credit: Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images | Kelley L Cox-Imagn Images The San Francisco 49ers haven’t needed to do anything regarding Brandon Aiyuk since they placed him on the Left Squad list in December 2025. That transaction immediately removed Aiyuk from the 53-man roster, and the team no longer has to pay him. Aiyuk’s contract was tolled, or paused. To return to the league, Aiyuk must formally apply for reinstatement. Per Over the Cap, a “ forfeitable breach ” of contract allowed the 49ers to recover portions of previously paid signing or option bonuses. According to multiple national reporters, Aiyuk is ready to return to the NFL — or at least attempt to. ESPN’s Adam Schefter tweeted that Aiyuk hired Drew Rosenhaus for representation. Rosenhaus said he is “working on getting him back to work and playing again in the NFL.” The 49ers don’t have to do anything. After Aiyuk spent the past offseason in a parasocial relationship with the Washington Commanders, he might not want to go to a team whose season is all but over. Washington does play in the NFC East, and that division is up for grabs. They also just lost Terry McLaurin, and Adam Peters is their general manager. After those social media antics, it’d be surprising to see a team offer Aiyuk anything more than a minimum contract. But it’s the NFL, and the Chiefs prove every month that they don’t care what kind of person they sign. So Aiyuk likely ends up in Kansas City if he’s granted his wish to be released. A wide receiver-needy team may be willing to part ways with a late conditional pick ahead of the trade deadline. The odds feel close to a long shot that we see Aiyuk on a football field again in 2026.

stories.title: Patriots unlikely to face Packers’ Micah Parsons even with practice return looming
stories.summary: While he is set to return, Parsons playing against the Patriots is not a done deal.
stories.detailText: The Green Bay Packers are getting some reinforcement ahead of their upcoming game with the New England Patriots. Micah Parsons, the four-time All-Pro edge rusher, is set to return to practice this week. Packers head coach Matt LaFleur announced the news on Monday. “That would be the intention,” he said during a press conference. “It’s going to be a process trying to get him back. We’re hopeful. It’s going to be dependent on the next couple of days, but we’re hopeful it’s going to be sometime this week.” Parsons, 27, started the regular season on the physically unable to perform list after tearing his ACL last December. When he went down, the Packers’ high-profile trade acquisition via the Dallas Cowboys had 12.5 sacks and a pair of forced fumbles on his 2025 résumé. While Parsons returning to practice opens the window for his return to Green Bay’s active roster and would make him eligible to play in Sunday’s contest in Foxborough, an immediate return to game action is not a guarantee. Last week, Rob Demovsky of ESPN noted that “[e]ven if Parsons practices next week, it would be highly unlikely he could play in the Week 9 game at the Patriots.” According to a report by NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport, Nov. 25 against the Los Angeles Rams is Parsons’ targeted return date. LeFleur hinted at that approach as well on Monday. “Like everything around here, it’s pretty fluid in terms of how he responds and just the progress he’s going to, hopefully, continue to make leading up to when he’s available,” he said. “If I had a bet on it, it’s going to be more toward the longer end than the shorter end.” For the Patriots, facing a Parsons-less Packers team is the preferred scenario. Even if not at a 100%, he has the ability to make game-changing plays against an offensive line that has had to deal with its fair share of injury questions this season. The Patriots have lost both of their starting guards to injury, while both of their tackles also got banged up at one point. Heading into Sunday’s game, New England’s projected O-line will feature Will Campbell and Morgan Moses at tackle, with two of Ben Brown, Matt Pryor and Walter Rouse flanking center Jared Wilson at the guard positions. Kickoff between the two storied franchise is scheduled for 4:25 p.m. ET on Sunday, Nov. 8.

stories.title: At 2-6, why is Shane Steichen sticking with Daniel Jones?
stories.summary: Is Indianapolis wasting Anthony Richardson Sr. career or was it self-sabotage?
stories.detailText: Indianapolis Colts quarterback Daniel Jones throws a pass during a training camp practice at Gand Park Sports Campus in Westfield, Ind. — August 10, 2025 | Thomas Butler-Guerrero It’s time to investigate for malpractice, no? Shane Steichen is deciding to stick with Daniel Jones as the Indianapolis Colts’ starting quarterback, he told reporters Monday. Apparently, getting whooped 42-7 in Jacksonville after 21 games with Jones was not enough to convince Indy’s fourth-year coach to make the same change he made after 10 starts with his first draft selection. I’m not here to say Jones is the whole problem in Indianapolis, but you’re wrong, Shane. Jones is halfway through the least-efficient season of his eight-year NFL career. In eight games, the veteran quarterback has career-lows in completion rate (60%) and passer rating (68.7), with just five passing touchdowns against nine interceptions and 12 total turnovers. Since signing with Indy, Jones has scored 30 total touchdowns against 17 interceptions. Steichen explained his decision by mentioning “it goes back to the preparation at the command he has of the offense”, doubling down saying that he believes Jones gives the Colts the best chance to win right now. #Colts HC Shane Steichen, asked if Daniel Jones is held to a softer standard: “It goes back to the preparation and the command he has of the offense. …” “You want to have accountability, but like I said, I feel in this situation that he gives us the best chance to win.” pic.twitter.com/2jsFHaf1Jk — James Boyd (@RomeovilleKid) November 2, 2026 Somebody slam the buzzer, because once again, you’re wrong. Indianapolis sits at 2-6 after four consecutive defeats, coming off their worst performance in Duval County. The Colts have lost 13 of their last 15 games dating back to the 2025 collapse, while Jones has lost nine of his last 11 starts. Reminder that Richardson is 8-7 in 15 career starts. The Colts have already begun the fire sale, trading cornerstone All-Pros Quenton Nelson (2027 third, 2028 fifth) to Seattle and DeForest Buckner (2027 fourth) to San Francisco for future draft compensation. Whatever playoff aspirations that remained by Halloween have effectively disappeared overnight. The Colts have waved the white flag in 2026, so there is a legitimate argument to start Anthony Richardson in the final year of his rookie contract. I was in attendance for every training camp practice at Grand Park Sports Campus in Westfield, and will start off by saying the continued concerns were obvious. Richardson struggled with handling snaps, pre-snap reads and the finer details of operating an NFL offense. Jones was absolutely running Steichen’s run-pass-option offensive scheme better, with the starters of course. Richardson was stuck competing for the backup job while competing with the second unit, and most of the time with the third unit. Indy’s lack of development with Richardson will at some point be a talking point on what exactly not to do. Those concerns haven’t magically disappeared, but at some point, the young quarterback has to get out of timeout and learn on the fly. Remember how rusty Richardson looked after essentially losing his rookie season? That’s how rusty Jones looks now and it’s midway through the season. Development demands playing time, and Indianapolis has done very little to give its former fourth overall pick a legitimate opportunity to get out of the dog house. Richardson offers a different look that Jones simply does not have off a torn Achilles. Richardson’s athleticism, mobility, arm strength and capability to threaten defenses with his legs and his arms is something that opponents “foam at the mouth at” when facing the Colts today. Those are the words from star running back Jonathan Taylor after the punishing loss on Sunday. Sure, Jones is more comfortable running play-action and run-pass-option concepts that have become Steichen’s bread and butter, but this scheme is not producing results. The Colts allowed six touchdowns on Sunday, while their offense has scored just five touchdowns combined over the last four games. Jones is getting pulverized, struggling to push the football downfield and repeatedly putting the defense in short fields with too many turnovers. There’s Indy’s $100M financial commitment to Jones from 2025 through 2027, but at this point, that investment can’t continue to dictate who plays quarterback. Ed Dodds needs to pull a Moneyball style trade to send Daniel Jones or Anthony Richardson Sr. to Baltimore, at least he will do what’s best for the organization moving forward. The Colts have four games before their bye week, with the struggling Dallas defense coming into town. Steichen might believe Jones gives Indianapolis the best chance to win right now, but the better question is why is Jones given a different leash than Richardson, who was benched after 10 NFL starts.

stories.title: Mike Vrabel remains confident in Andy Borregales despite missed kicks
stories.summary: Borregales missed his third field goal on Sunday.
stories.detailText: Andy Borregales made just one of his two field goal attempts in the New England Patriots’ Week 8 victroy over the Miami Dolphins on Sunday. The miss came from just 40 yards out, marking Borregales’ third missed field goal of the season from inside 50 yards. Through eight games, the second-year kicker is now 10-of-13 on field goals and 20-of-21 on extra points. Head coach Mike Vrabel, however, still has belief in his kicker. “That needs to get corrected,” Vrabel said Monday. “I’ve got a lot of confidence in Andy. I think when you see the timing and when the approach is in rhythm, it looks really good. We have to make our kicks. Everybody has a job here. There’s no real message. It’s, ‘Hey, we’ve got to make them.’ But I’ve got a lot of confidence. “I thought he did a really nice job on the kickoff with the ball placement. Hopefully, he’s making a lot of extra points and not having to kick a lot of field goals.” The Patriots selected Borregales in the sixth round of the 2025 NFL Draft out of the University of Miami. His rookie season got off to a slow start, including a pair of missed extra points in Miami in Week 2. However, he missed just three kicks over the remainder of the regular season. During his weekly appearance on WEEI’s The Greg Hill Show , Vrabel also poked fun at how quickly analysts and fans call for players to be benched or released after making mistakes, referencing both Drake Maye and Rhamondre Stevenson as examples. The Patriots have not had internal competition on the roster for Borregales since his rookie season, when John Parker Romo competed with him during training camp. For now, Vrabel appears content to stick with his kicker while emphasizing the need for better results.

stories.title: Rams see surprising name move up edge depth chart
stories.summary: Undrafted rookie helps L.A. fill the Myles Garrett void
stories.detailText: It wasn’t a thing of beauty , but the Los Angles Rams stacked a second straight win on Sunday, knocking off their housemates, the Los Angeles Chargers, 24-9. L.A. evened their record at 4-4 and while the offense is struggling with finding depth to move the needle for injured playmakers, the defense is developing contributing backups. One such player is edge Wesley Bailey, an undrafted Rams rookie from Louisville. Bailey’s college profile read as a highly athletic prospect with NFL frame, length, and motor, but raw technical skills and an unrefined toolbox of moves. L.A, started him out slowly, active but only a couple of special teams reps in Week 1, then a lane opened up for him with the Myles Garrett injury . Bailey has made the most of the break. On Sunday he had his biggest workload of the season, 32 reps (52%). For the day, he logged five tackles, a pressure, and had the sweet fourth quarter strip sack. You can see his growth in both game logs and on the field, consistently getting more reps and incrementally adding production. Still in the learning phase, he’’ll need to get get better at setting the edge and dropping into flat coverage, but his twitch and effort clearly stand out on film. He’s proven to be a solid value at the league minimum salary. Here’s a review of the snap counts from Sunday. Players, their snap counts and percentage of play time in bold. Quarterback Matthew Stafford (54, 100%) Stafford really appears to be bothered by pass rush pressure this season and it seems out of character with his fearless, gunslinger nature. He was effective on the quick underneath throws, but when forced to hold the ball and read, struggled with accuracy. The Rams have to figure out a way to allow him time to stretch the field and not let the passing game continue to be compressed. Running back Blake Corum (17, 31%) Kyren Williams (37, 69%) Another ham and egg performance, the duo combined for 27 carries, 129 yards, and two touchdowns. Both have over a 50 percent success rate for the season. Through Weeks 1 through 6, Williams was the clear RB#1, getting 70% of snaps, 64% of touches, and 65% of yards. Now it appears that the two are alternating full drives, while KWill is still getting more snaps, Corum’s touches and production are very similar. Blake Corum with the smooth move and TD! LACvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/YP3lqMMQYg — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Wide receiver Puka Nacua (52, 96%) Konata Mumpfield (27, 50%) Tutu Atwell (21, 39%) Jordan Whittington (4, 7%) CJ Daniels (2, 4%) Nacua (368) passed Robert Woods for #9 on the Rams all-time receptions list. Atwell contributed an explosive play. Completed or not, the Rams should throw 2-3 of those per game, if only to loosen up the underneath areas. Mumpfield continues to be a non-entity in the passing game, getting the bulk of snaps, but few targets and even less production. Whittington’s offensive reps continue to trend down. Daniels got to mop up work as the Rams went into victory formation. Tight end Tyler Higbee (45, 83%) Davis Allen (40, 74%) Max Klare (25, 46%) Tight end usage flip-flopped at halftime. Rams used multiple tight ends on 25 percent of reps in the first half and upped it to nearly 70 percent in the final 30 minutes. Blocking was the word of the day, the unit was targeted only four times with three catches for 28 yards. Higbee had a couple of concentration penalties. Watch replays of the Rams touchdown runs, Allen is a part of most of them. Klare received substantial worthwhile reps, mostly blocking, but he did get out on a few routes. Offensive line Alaric Jackson, Steve Avila, Coleman Shelton, Kevin Dotson, Warren McClendon (all 54, 100%) 52.6 percent of their designed runs coming out of man/duo blocking schemes, highest in the NFL. On those plays, the Rams put up Top 10 in yards per carry, success rate, and explosive run rate. Early in Sunday’s game, the line gave up a lot of pressure, but settled down in the second half. Coming out of the gate with a stronger commitment to the run game could help alleviate this. Special teams Shaky at best, but with nothing glaringly damaging. This may be the best case scenario for the rest of the season. Defensive line Braden Fiske (45, 74%) Aaron Donald (40, 66%) Ty Hamilton (25, 41%) Tyler Davis (20, 33%) Larrell Murchison (19, 31%) The Rams defensive line is doing quite well making up the voids of Kobie Turner and Poona Ford. Some of it is the level of competition, but good work is good work. Donald is getting into game shape, his pressure and quick pressure rates are rising weekly. Fiske appears to be getting more pressures. Hamilton has raised his play time in three straight weeks and looks sound, particularly when lined up as a nose tackle. Davis’ reps went down from the past three weeks. Murchison’s usage has been edging up since being called up from the practice squad. Edge Byron Young (46, 75%) Josaiah Stewart (34, 56%) Wesley Bailey (32, 52%) Darryl Peterson ( 15, 25%) Young was quieter than normal, but Stewart played better than he has in weeks. Looked very active and provided some nice pressure and run stops. Bailey looks to have distanced himself as E#3. Peterson had a big jump in snaps, but didn’t record a stat. Ball went out of bounds, but this forced fumble from Wesley Bailey was 🔥 LACvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/sJhAgAK9nr — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Off-ball linebacker Nate Landman (42, 69%) Omar Speights (35, 57%) I thought Speight played well for the second week in a row. Landman didn’t have the green dot on Sunday, wonder if this is a one-off occurrence or if the Rams see that subbing him out for big dime personnel groupings is a better against short passing offenses. Safety Kamren Curl (61, 100%) Quentin Lake (61, 100%) Kamren Kinchens (33, 54%) Jaylen McCollough (15, 25%) L.A. is using dime personnel (six defensive backs) packages at a league-leading 43 percent. Lake is lining up primarily deep or at linebacker and playing less in the slot this year. The Rams are doing a good job of getting him lined up against tight ends, a matchup that he’s best suited to. Curl quietly is third on the team in tackles and tackles for loss. Kinchens had a season low in snaps, while his play percentage is down this season, he brings excellent tackle production per snap. McCollough’s snaps were down as well. It makes sense to sub him onto the field for either of the linebackers in any down/distance situation with four yards to go. Cornerback Trent McDuffie (49, 80%) Jaylen Watson (41, 67%) Josh Wallace (41, 67%) Emmanuel Forbes (17, 28%) L.A. has really leaned into using man coverage at 37.6 percent, second most in the NFL. How good have McDuffie and Watson been? Both are in the NFL’s Top 5 for least completion percentage allowed for cornerbacks. What’s really outstanding is their ability and willingness in run defense. Wallace got beat for an explosive, but over his 2026 body of work has been solid. Forbes has found a role as a backup in the the new-look secondary. Trent McDuffie with the TFL 💪 LACvsLAR on FOX/FOX One Stream on @NFLPlus pic.twitter.com/tLUs5vekkg — NFL (@NFL) November 1, 2026 Going forward Hard to argue that the Rams have turned the corner. In the midst of a five-game weak spot in the schedule, they are 2-1 and need to finish this track at 5-1. Next Sunday, the Washington Commanders, on their home turf, should provide a test. Standing at 4-4, fans will have to stay optimistic and watch the standings/playoff seedings. Parity will keep the wildcard openings within reach, but the Rams will have to stack wins, ugly or not.

stories.title: Week 8 Observations: First Loss, Same Problems
stories.summary: Excuses Are No Longer Acceptable
stories.detailText: DETROIT,MICHIGAN-OCTOBER 25: Head coach Kevin O'Connell of the Minnesota Vikings looks on from the sidelines during an NFL football game between the New York Jets and the Detroit Lions in Detroit, Michigan USA, on Sunday, September 27, 2026 (Photo by Amy Lemus/NurPhoto via Getty Images) | NurPhoto via Getty Images First and foremost, prayers for Detroit Lions linebacker Jack Campbell. As of this writing, all I’m seeing is that he was taken to the hospital and is being evaluated for a neck injury. Wishing for very good news soon. When something like this happens, it puts meaningless complaints about the team and gameplay into perspective. Get well, Jack Campbell, and hoping for a full recovery. We’re all Lions fans now. Vikings Get Their Reality Check The Minnesota Vikings lost a game they deserved to lose. Our winning was unsustainable, and today’s outcome was predictable once the competition improved. There would inevitably come a time when Flores and special teams couldn’t carry the team to victory. That day came at Ford Field in Week 8. The offense failed the test. We’re now 6-1 and facing considerable headwinds: a ridiculously underachieving offense, a dominant defense that has recently shown vulnerabilities against the run, Will Reichard suddenly missing kicks, and an absolutely brutal upcoming stretch of games. This is not the time to focus on the defense or the kicker. Both will be fine. The former spent nearly 36 minutes on the field. Fatigue lays the foundation for missed tackles, and the Vikings had double digits in the second half. They may also have been (justifiably) pressing for a turnover first, since our offense is about as reliable as a cheap paper umbrella. Jahmyr Gibbs being the best running back in football didn’t help. In the end, despite the Lions rushing for 230 yards, Jared Goff was sacked four times and held to a Vikings-esque 176 yards passing. The Lions were held to 5-for-13 on third down and scored 19 points at home, despite averaging 31 points per game coming into the game. Meanwhile, Will Reichard remains a superhero in my book. Not a concern. Mere hiccups for the king of aura, vibes, and stellar hair. The Offense Has Run Out of Excuses Last week, I gave the offense this week and next against a similarly porous Bills defense to get things right. And by “right,” I meant sniffing 30 points. After another week in which even 17 was out of reach, I’m moving it up. I’m now ready to slam the ejection-seat button. #Vikings offense this season: • 29th in yards per game • 30th in passing yards per game • 31st in offensive TDs per game • 27th in PPG • 27th on 3rd down • 28th in yards per play • 32nd in first downs per game pic.twitter.com/mEIrNzcsEc — Ari Meirov (@MySportsUpdate) November 1, 2026 In 20 quarters as a starter, the Kyler Murray-led Vikings offense is averaging just 17 points per game. He has just 5 TDs and 3 INTs, with two of the passing touchdowns coming because Justin Jefferson was ridiculous. After the Saints’ game inspired confidence, things were about to turn around; they haven’t. His QBR for the Lions game was only 36.8. Nothing looks easy right now. Everything is a slog. The passing game is an occasional T.J. Hockenson seam-route catch that breaks up a series of three-and-outs. Yes, it’s an exaggeration, but it’s rooted in some truth. I was really excited about the Murray signing in the spring because of the dual-threat capability we haven’t had consistently for over 20 years. With a few highlights here and there, that hasn’t materialized as I envisioned, either. Coming into today's game, the Lions had allowed more passing yards and more passing touchdowns than any team in the NFL. Midway through the third quarter, Kyler Murray has 86 passing yards. At some point, it is, indeed, his fault. — The Daily Norseman (@DailyNorseman) November 1, 2026 There are three possibilities. Scenario A is that Kevin O’Connell is putting Murray in advantageous situations to score 24+ points a game, but Murray is repeatedly failing to execute the offense efficiently. Scenario B is that, more often than not, KOC hasn’t put Murray in a position to succeed by maximizing his skill set and adjusting the play calling to his strengths. Scenario C is that it’s a little bit of both. I suspect the last one, if a little bit more A than B. Regardless, the responsibility to fix it falls to KOC, the head coach and de facto offensive coordinator. If it’s A, he owes it to the rest of the team to see what Carson Wentz can do. If it’s B, he needs to swallow his pride, own his mistakes, and step out of his comfort zone. If it’s C, they need to work together to find the quickest viable way to meet in the middle and get things rolling right away. Like tomorrow. Or today. Better yet, yesterday. But what’s with the urgency? We’re 6-1! It’s only Week 8; there’s plenty of time! Umm, no. There really isn’t. Two playoff spots go to the winners of the NFC East and South, leaving five spots for the following seven teams: Vikings, Lions, Packers, Bears, 49ers, Seahawks, and Rams. A 10-7 record might not be enough this year. More on this in a bit. Either way, outside help at quarterback seems unlikely. The only viable plug-and-play trade target is Kirk Cousins. The Raiders’ eyes would light up if Nolan Teasley’s name appeared on the caller ID. They’d hold all the cards, and given our desperation, the price could likely be prohibitive. And that’s assuming they’d even do it, since at 4-4 they’re still theoretically alive for the playoffs in a competitive AFC and Cousins is having a strong season. Hey, if there’s one silver lining this week, at least we didn’t lose and didn’t have to watch J.J. McCarthy lead the Giants to another victory. Next week? All bets are off. You couldn’t have botched the QB situation any worse than the Vikings have over the past three seasons. It’s truly something to behold. 6-4 Incoming? Spoiler for my Week 9 game preview in a few days: I can’t pick the Vikings to beat any top-tier team right now, given how this offense is playing. What’s the point of doing these articles if I’m not honest? There’s a real chance the Bills beat us comfortably in front of a nationwide audience on Monday night. Josh Allen is the most difficult quarterback in the NFL to defend. Playing at Lambeau Field is never easy, and it’s on a short week. Then comes the 6-1 49ers on a neutral field, with Brock Purdy playing like an MVP. Looking at 6-4 on November 23rd is a distinct possibility, and memories of 2003 would shift from a whisper to a bullhorn in all directions. You are what your record says you are until your record catches up with who you really are. I’m afraid we may be in that boat, and I’m not the only one thinking so. Without saying a word, Justin Jefferson’s expressions throughout the game spoke volumes, as did his decision not to address the media afterward. Silence is often the most effective form of communication. He deserves better. The Super Bowl-caliber defense and special teams deserve better. This locker room likely doesn’t reflect a 6-1 team. Right now, the “QB Whisperer” is a 5-star restaurant serving cold pizza and stale French fries. If your goal is to raise a playoff participation banner at U.S. Bank Stadium next September, possibly sneaking into the playoffs and being one-and-done, then this team is for you. If you want to actually win a Super Bowl, something drastic has to happen at QB right away. We’ve already squandered the bye week that would’ve bought us time. If that means scrapping the 2022-2026 modern West Coast offense playbook and starting over with plays tailored to Murray’s unique strengths and comfort level, fine. If it’s benching Murray for Wentz, fine. If it’s bringing Cousins in here before the deadline, fine. The status quo is no longer acceptable, and the excuses jar is empty. Fix it.

stories.summary: It looks like this week will, in fact, be the week for Micah Parsons to return to practice.
stories.detailText: It looks like this week will, in fact, be the week for Micah Parsons to return to practice. Head coach Matt LaFleur told reporters in his Monday press conference that it's the team's "intention" to have Parsons return to practice. “Again, it’s going to be a process trying to get him back ,” LaFleur said. “But we’re hopeful that — it’s going to be dependent upon the next couple of days. But, we’re hopeful that he’ll be able to get out there sometime this week.” The Packers had meetings and a walk-through on Monday after defeating the Panthers last Thursday night. LaFleur noted Parsons was with trainers during that session, explaining why Parsons has not yet been designated to return. But even once Parsons returns to the field, Green Bay isn’t expecting him to play right away. The club plans to use a good portion of the 21-day window to activate him off of the physically unable to perform list. “I would just say, like everything around here, it’s pretty fluid in terms of how he responds and just the progress he’s going to, hopefully, continue to make leading up to when he’s available,” LaFleur said. “If I had a bet on it, it’s going to be more toward the longer end than the shorter end.” Parsons suffered a torn ACL late last season. Multiple reports over the weekend indicated the Packers are targeting Week 12 for his return, which would be the “Thanksgiving Eve” game against the Rams in Los Angeles.

stories.title: Cowboys offense failed to capitalize on defensive stops
stories.summary: The Cowboys offense failed on Sunday
stories.detailText: Mandatory Credit: Kevin Jairaj-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The Dallas Cowboys defense is not good at football. Relying on the defense would be a horrible strategy. Nothing about the state of the defense surprises us anymore which means that capitalizing on the moments where they are successful is of the highest priority. The Cowboys did not do that against the Arizona Cardinals. Dallas squandered the defense’s stops On the surface it seems like the Cowboys offense did enough to win the game on Sunday. They scored 30 points, after all. But those 30 points are a little misleading. Consider that one of the Cowboys’ touchdowns came after Shemar James returned an interception to the Arizona 5-yard line. That wasn’t a ton of work to cash in. What we are interested in looking at here is how the offense performed in moments like that, off of stops generated by the defense. There were six in total. In sequence: Cardinals Punt……………… Cowboys Turnover on Downs Cardinals Interception downed at Arizona 5-yard line… Cowboys TD Cardinals Punt………………. Cowboys TD Cardinals Fumble…………. Cowboys Missed Field Goal Cardinals Punt………………. Cowboys Punt Cardinals Punt (OT)………. Cowboys Punt Of the six instances in question the Cowboys offense successfully capitalized just twice, and it only required them to travel a handful of yards as noted. What’s more is it only even happened because of a fumble recovery in the endzone after Javonte Williams had the ball pop loose. The point here is that the Cowboys offense was given six opportunities by their defense to make the opponent pay. They hardly delivered in that respect. Their 30-point performance is a little hollow in that way, and a little might be generous. These are the moments that you have to capitalize on in general in football, but especially when everyone understands that your defense is what the Cowboys’ is this season. Obviously they did not and they paid the price for that.

stories.title: Matt LaFleur says Packers will stick with running back Josh Jacobs
stories.summary: The Packers are waiting to see what the NFL will do before making any moves with Josh Jacobs.
stories.detailText: GREEN BAY, WISCONSIN - OCTOBER 29: Josh Jacobs #8 of the Green Bay Packers looks on against the Carolina Panthers during the national anthem prior to an NFL football game at Lambeau Field on October 29, 2026 in Green Bay, Wisconsin. (Photo by Michael Owens/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Packers are addressing the still-unfolding Josh Jacobs situation by not saying much. During his Monday press availability, Matt LaFleur addressed the additional allegations of abuse levied by multiple women against the running back by saying he didn’t have much to say. “Obviously, we’re aware of the prior allegations on Josh and we’re going to allow the NFL to do its process, but I would anticipate him being a member of us moving forward,” LaFleur said. “That’s really all I have to speak on [that].” Jacobs entered a no-contest plea in his abuse and criminal damage case earlier this year, and the additional allegations came to light after the Hobart/Lawrence Police Department released documents pertaining to Jacobs’ 2026 arrest . The additional allegations date to 2022 and 2021, when Jacobs was a member of the Las Vegas Raiders. Jacobs spent six weeks on the Commissioner Exempt list earlier this season. He was not fined and could still be suspended. The NFL has yet to issue a definitive ruling on his case, possibly because video footage of the incident resulting in Jacobs’ arrest in May still has not been released — and may never be. General manager Brian Gutekunst has yet to speak publicly on Jacobs’ situation (he typically addresses the media just once during the season after the conclusion of training camp), but LaFleur’s remarks make the Packers’ position pretty clear: they’re not going to do anything until the NFL makes its own ruling. Jacobs has been central to the Packers’ backfield operation since he returned, playing more than 52% of the Packers’ snaps in their Week 7 loss to the Lions, then lining up for 71% of their snaps in their Week 8 win over the Panthers. He’s carried 32 times for 75 yards and a touchdown while catching 11 passes for 68 yards and a touchdown in those two games.

stories.detailText: More allegations of domestic violence against Packers running back Josh Jacobs surfaced late last week and head coach Matt LaFleur addressed them at the start of his press conference on Monday. Jacobs missed the first six games of the season while on the Commissioner Exempt list after he pleaded no contest to misdemeanor battery and criminal damage related to a May arrest and the other allegations were made to police in the wake of that arrest. The NFL said in a statement on Saturday that those allegations will be reviewed as part of its ongoing investigation into Jacobs's conduct and LaFleur said that the team will "just let the process play out" without any change to Jacobs's current status. “Obviously we're aware of the prior allegations on Josh," LaFleur said. "We're going to allow the NFL to do its process, but I would anticipate him being a member of us moving forward. That’s really all I have to speak on.” Jacobs drew attention last Thursday with a touchdown celebration that appeared to mimic being placed in handcuffs. Jacobs offered an alternate explanation and LaFleur said that he had a conversation with the back about being more aware of the optics surrounding such choices, but declined to offer any other details of their discussion.
